1	---
2	status: Accepted
3	date: 2026-11-20
4	decision-makers: Felipe Sabogal (accepted at HC2, 2026-11-20), architect subagent (proposal)
5	consulted: specs/US-01/spec.md v0.2 (Approved), specs/US-02/story.md, specs/US-03/story.md, MDN Web Docs (Window.sessionStorage)
6	informed: all agents via CLAUDE.md precedence
7	---
8	
9	# ADR-0003: Front-end persistence of the wizard state
10	
11	## Context and Problem Statement
12	
13	The wizard keeps the step 1 values (US-01), later the chosen plan (US-02), between steps and must
14	not send them to any server. The person must find their data when going back (US-01-AC-04,
15	US-01-AC-20) and, after a rejected payment, "try again without losing my information" (US-03
16	story). The values include personal data: the document number and the birth date. We must decide
17	where the state lives, what is stored, how it is scoped per country, and when it is cleared
18	(US-01-Q-15, answered "decided by the ADR; sessionStorage is the starting point", and
19	US-01-Q-02, default accepted).
20	
21	## Decision Drivers
22	
23	- D1. "Use a front-end strategy to persist the data; a database is not required." (source: Assessment; US-01-BR-08)
24	- D2. Data kept when going back, in-app and with browser back (US-01-AC-04, US-01-AC-20) and across a reload in the same tab, proposed by US-01-Q-15 (US-01-AC-21).
25	- D3. Data never crosses countries; opening another country's context discards the previous one (US-01-BR-07, US-01-AC-22, US-01-Q-02).
26	- D4. Privacy: document number and birth date are personal data (US-01-Q-15; spec §9 security/privacy). Step 1 values are never sent to a server or written to logs (US-01-AC-27, CLAUDE.md §3). Masking in the summary (US-03 story: "The document number is shown partially masked").
27	- D5. A changed configuration must not resurrect values of removed fields or options (US-01-Q-16, US-01-AC-23).
28	- D6. Retry after a failed payment keeps the data; a successful payment ends the quote (US-03 story: "Rejected payment", "Successful payment").
29	- D7. "Use fictitious data only." (source: Assessment). Tests and fixtures use only seed values.
30	
31	## Considered Options
32	
33	1. **In memory only** (a signal store, lost on reload).
34	2. **`sessionStorage`**, one versioned entry, scoped to one country, cleared on country change,
35	   tab close and successful payment.
36	3. **`localStorage` with an expiry** (for example 30 minutes), same shape.
37	4. **Hybrid**: `sessionStorage` for non-sensitive values, document number and birth date in
38	   memory only.
39	
40	## Decision Outcome
41	
42	Chosen option: **"2. sessionStorage"**, because it is the only option that survives a reload in
43	the same tab (D2) while being deleted by the browser when the tab closes, and its per-tab
44	partitioning keeps a CO tab and a CL tab from overwriting each other (D3). The privacy cost
45	(personal data in clear text in the tab's storage) is bounded by the tab lifetime and the
46	clearing rules below (D4).
47	
48	### What is decided
49	
50	**Store and storage key**
51	
52	- A root-provided `QuoteStore` (signals) is the single owner of the wizard state. Components and
53	  guards never touch `sessionStorage` directly.
54	- One `sessionStorage` entry, key `quote-wizard`, value JSON:
55	  `{ "version": 1, "country": "<code>", "step1": { "values": { "<key>": <value> } }, "plan": … }`.
56	  `values` holds the **raw editing values** of the form model: strings for `text`, `number`,
57	  `select` and `date`, booleans for `checkbox`, and `''` for an empty field. An in-progress
58	  invalid value such as `'2015.5'` is stored as typed. The spec §7.3 typed output (`text` →
59	  trimmed string, `number` → integer, `select` → option value, `date` → `YYYY-MM-DD`, `checkbox`
60	  → boolean, unchecked optional checkbox → `false`, empty optional → `null`) is produced only on a
61	  valid "Continuar"; that typed output is what US-02 and US-03 consume. `plan` is added by US-02
62	  (an identifier of the chosen plan only, defined in its spec).
63	- **Not stored**: the field configuration, labels, option labels, plans, prices or terms. They are
64	  fetched once per full page load (US-01-Q-16, ADR-0001) and later steps read labels from that
65	  in-memory configuration. This settles the open point in spec §7.3 ("Whether it is stored or
66	  refetched is a persistence ADR detail"): refetched.
67	- **Never written to storage**: payment data (US-03), if the simulated payment asks for any. It
68	  lives only in the payment component's memory.
69	- No cookies, no `localStorage`, no IndexedDB for wizard data.
70	
71	**When it is written**
72	
73	- On every change of a step 1 value, the raw editing values are written (the store writes
74	  synchronously after updating its signal), so a reload restores exactly what the person typed,
75	  valid or not. The values are revalidated when shown and on "Continuar" (US-01-Q-16); only a
76	  valid "Continuar" produces the §7.3 typed output.
77	
78	**When it is read**
79	
80	- Once, when the store is created (each full page load). The JSON is validated at the boundary:
81	  wrong `version`, invalid JSON, a `country` that is not an alpha-2 code, or values of an
82	  unexpected type → the entry is discarded and a `console.warn` without any value is logged.
83	- When step 1 renders with the configuration of this page load: values whose key is no longer
84	  configured are dropped from the state, and a `select` value whose option no longer exists is
85	  cleared (US-01-AC-23). The pruned state is written back.
86	
87	**Scope per country (US-01-Q-02)**
88	
89	- The entry holds at most **one** country. When a supported country's context is entered
90	  (ADR-0001, `/:country` route) and the stored `country` differs, the entry is deleted before
91	  step 1 renders. Visiting `/` or an unknown country does not delete it.
92	- `sessionStorage` is partitioned by origin and by tab (MDN: "partitioned by both origin and
93	  browser tabs (top-level browsing contexts)"), so two tabs with different countries have
94	  independent state.
95	
96	**When it is cleared**
97	
98	| Event | Effect | Owner |
99	|---|---|---|
100	| Tab or window closed | Browser deletes it (MDN: "Closing the tab/window ends the session and clears the data in `sessionStorage`.") | Browser |
101	| Another supported country's context entered | Entry deleted | US-01 (`QuoteStore`, called from the `/:country` route) |
102	| Successful payment | Entry deleted before the confirmation is shown; the confirmation keeps only the simulated quote number in memory | US-03 |
103	| Rejected payment | **Nothing** cleared: the person retries with the same data | US-03 |
104	| Unreadable or wrong-version entry | Entry deleted | US-01 |
105	
106	**Privacy rules**
107	
108	- Values are never logged (no `console.*` with values, warnings name keys only), never sent in a
109	  request (US-01-AC-27), never put in the URL, and never in the document title.
110	- The full document number is stored, because US-03 masks it **at display time**; the masked form
111	  is never stored separately.
112	- No client-side encryption: the key would live in the same JavaScript as the data, so it would
113	  add complexity without protecting against the realistic threat (script injection in the page).
114	  The protection is the tab lifetime, the clearing rules and the absence of third-party scripts.
115	- If `sessionStorage` is unavailable (blocked by the browser, quota exceeded), the store keeps the
116	  state in memory only and logs one `console.warn`; the wizard still works except across reloads.
117	
118	### Consequences
119	
120	- Good, because the person keeps their data across steps, browser back and a reload (D2), and
121	  after a rejected payment (D6).
122	- Good, because the data disappears with the tab, with a country switch and after payment (D3, D4).
123	- Good, because one entry with a version number and boundary validation makes later stories'
124	  additions (plan) and format changes safe.
125	- Bad, because the document number and birth date sit in clear text in the tab's storage while
126	  the tab is open, readable by any script running on the origin and by anyone using the same
127	  browser tab — mitigation: no third-party scripts, values never logged, cleared on payment and
128	  country switch; the residual risk is accepted for a quote flow without accounts.
129	- Bad, because MDN notes the page session "survives over page reloads and restores", so a browser
130	  that restores a crashed or reopened session may bring the data back — mitigation: accepted;
131	  the data stays on the same device and profile.
132	- Bad, because a tab opened from the wizard tab may start with a copy of its storage (MDN: with an
133	  `opener`, "the `sessionStorage` is initially a copy of the opener's") — mitigation: the app opens
134	  no new windows; copies are independent afterwards.
135	- Bad, because writing on every change stores invalid intermediate values — mitigation: they are
136	  revalidated on display and on "Continuar"; the AC-19 guard validates before step 2.
137	- Neutral: spec US-01-AC-21 ("Data survives a reload") stays as written; the "memory only"
138	  rewrite foreseen in the spec does not apply.
139	
140	### Strongest argument against
141	
142	The document number and birth date stay in clear text in the tab's storage for as long as the
143	tab is open, readable by any script running on the origin. MDN states that the page session
144	"survives over page reloads and restores", so a browser that restores a crashed or reopened
145	session can bring that personal data back. Option 1 (memory only) avoids all of this: nothing
146	personal is ever written to the device. Its only cost is that a reload loses the data.
147	
148	**Why we accept it:** losing everything on a reload, which users do on mobile and after errors,
149	fails the reload behaviour approved for AC-21 (D2), and the AC-19 guard would send the person
150	back to an empty step 1. The exposure is limited: no third-party scripts, values are never
151	logged, the entry is cleared on payment and on country switch, and the data stays on the same
152	device and browser profile. The residual risk is accepted for a quote flow without accounts.
153	
154	### Confirmation
155	
156	- Unit tests `quote-store.spec.ts`: the raw editing values (including an in-progress invalid
157	  value such as `'2015.5'`) are persisted on every change, and a new store instance restores them
158	  exactly from `sessionStorage` (AC-21); the §7.3 typed output (AC-18) is produced only on a valid
159	  "Continuar", never on an invalid one; entering another country deletes the entry and the original
160	  country is empty afterwards (AC-22); removed keys and options are pruned (AC-23); a corrupted or
161	  wrong-version entry is discarded with a warning that contains no value; storage unavailable →
162	  memory fallback.
163	- E2E `us-01-country-context.spec.ts` (AC-22) and `us-01-security.spec.ts` (AC-27, no value in any
164	  request).
165	- Review checklist: only `QuoteStore` references `sessionStorage`; no `localStorage`, cookies or
166	  IndexedDB for wizard data; no `console.*` call receives a value; US-03 clears the entry on
167	  successful payment and not on a rejected one.
168	
169	## Pros and Cons of the Options
170	
171	### 1. In memory only
172	
173	- Good, because nothing is written to the device; the strongest privacy option.
174	- Good, because it is the simplest to implement and test.
175	- Bad, because a reload, which users do on mobile and after errors, loses everything (fails the
176	  reload behaviour proposed in US-01-Q-15; AC-21 would be rewritten).
177	- Bad, because a reload on step 2 or 3 sends the person back to an empty step 1 through the AC-19
178	  guard.
179	
180	### 2. `sessionStorage` (chosen)
181	
182	- Good, because it survives reloads and is cleared by the browser when the tab closes.
183	- Good, because it is partitioned per tab, so different countries in different tabs do not clash.
184	- Bad, because personal data is in clear text while the tab is open.
185	- Bad, because browser session restore can bring it back.
186	
187	### 3. `localStorage` with an expiry
188	
189	- Good, because the person could close the tab and come back within the expiry.
190	- Bad, because the data outlives the tab, so on a shared computer the next person can see it; the
191	  expiry is only enforced when the app runs again.
192	- Bad, because `localStorage` is shared by all tabs of the origin: a CO tab and a CL tab would
193	  overwrite each other's state.
194	
195	### 4. Hybrid (sensitive values in memory only)
196	
197	- Good, because the document number and birth date never touch storage.
198	- Bad, because after a reload the person must re-enter exactly the most tedious fields, and the
199	  AC-19 guard sends them back to step 1 with a partially filled form; AC-21 would hold only for
200	  some fields.
201	- Bad, because which keys are sensitive is decided in code, while editors can add new fields
202	  (for example a phone number) that would silently be stored.
203	
204	## More Information
205	
206	- MDN Web Docs, `Window.sessionStorage`
207	  (https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Window/sessionStorage), read on 2026-11-20:
208	  lifetime ("survives over page reloads and restores"; "Closing the tab/window ends the session
209	  and clears the data"), partitioning by origin and tab, copy from an opener.
210	- Related ADRs: ADR-0001 (country context and the `/:country` route that triggers the switch),
211	  ADR-0002 (step 1 values never sent; AC-27), ADR-0004 (forms library, reserved: how the form is
212	  hydrated from the store).
213	- Revisit when: the product needs to resume a quote on another day or device (that needs a
214	  server, out of scope), or real personal data is processed (a privacy review would then be
215	  required).
216	- Clarified at HC2 (Felipe Sabogal, 2026-11-20): raw editing values in storage; §7.3 typed output
217	  only on a valid Continuar.

---
status: Accepted
date: 2026-11-20
decision-makers: Felipe Sabogal (accepted at HC2, 2026-11-20), architect subagent (proposal)
consulted: specs/US-01/spec.md v0.2 (Approved), specs/US-02/story.md, specs/US-03/story.md, MDN Web Docs (Window.sessionStorage)
informed: all agents via CLAUDE.md precedence
---

# ADR-0003: Front-end persistence of the wizard state

## Context and Problem Statement

The wizard keeps the step 1 values (US-01), later the chosen plan (US-02), between steps and must
not send them to any server. The person must find their data when going back (US-01-AC-04,
US-01-AC-20) and, after a rejected payment, "try again without losing my information" (US-03
story). The values include personal data: the document number and the birth date. We must decide
where the state lives, what is stored, how it is scoped per country, and when it is cleared
(US-01-Q-15, answered "decided by the ADR; sessionStorage is the starting point", and
US-01-Q-02, default accepted).

## Decision Drivers

- D1. "Use a front-end strategy to persist the data; a database is not required." (source: Assessment; US-01-BR-08)
- D2. Data kept when going back, in-app and with browser back (US-01-AC-04, US-01-AC-20) and across a reload in the same tab, proposed by US-01-Q-15 (US-01-AC-21).
- D3. Data never crosses countries; opening another country's context discards the previous one (US-01-BR-07, US-01-AC-22, US-01-Q-02).
- D4. Privacy: document number and birth date are personal data (US-01-Q-15; spec §9 security/privacy). Step 1 values are never sent to a server or written to logs (US-01-AC-27, CLAUDE.md §3). Masking in the summary (US-03 story: "The document number is shown partially masked").
- D5. A changed configuration must not resurrect values of removed fields or options (US-01-Q-16, US-01-AC-23).
- D6. Retry after a failed payment keeps the data; a successful payment ends the quote (US-03 story: "Rejected payment", "Successful payment").
- D7. "Use fictitious data only." (source: Assessment). Tests and fixtures use only seed values.

## Considered Options

1. **In memory only** (a signal store, lost on reload).
2. **`sessionStorage`**, one versioned entry, scoped to one country, cleared on country change,
   tab close and successful payment.
3. **`localStorage` with an expiry** (for example 30 minutes), same shape.
4. **Hybrid**: `sessionStorage` for non-sensitive values, document number and birth date in
   memory only.

## Decision Outcome

Chosen option: **"2. sessionStorage"**, because it is the only option that survives a reload in
the same tab (D2) while being deleted by the browser when the tab closes, and its per-tab
partitioning keeps a CO tab and a CL tab from overwriting each other (D3). The privacy cost
(personal data in clear text in the tab's storage) is bounded by the tab lifetime and the
clearing rules below (D4).

### What is decided

**Store and storage key**

- A root-provided `QuoteStore` (signals) is the single owner of the wizard state. Components and
  guards never touch `sessionStorage` directly.
- One `sessionStorage` entry, key `quote-wizard`, value JSON:
  `{ "version": 1, "country": "<code>", "step1": { "values": { "<key>": <value> } }, "plan": … }`.
  `values` holds the **raw editing values** of the form model: strings for `text`, `number`,
  `select` and `date`, booleans for `checkbox`, and `''` for an empty field. An in-progress
  invalid value such as `'2015.5'` is stored as typed. The spec §7.3 typed output (`text` →
  trimmed string, `number` → integer, `select` → option value, `date` → `YYYY-MM-DD`, `checkbox`
  → boolean, unchecked optional checkbox → `false`, empty optional → `null`) is produced only on a
  valid "Continuar"; that typed output is what US-02 and US-03 consume. `plan` is added by US-02
  (an identifier of the chosen plan only, defined in its spec).
- **Not stored**: the field configuration, labels, option labels, plans, prices or terms. They are
  fetched once per full page load (US-01-Q-16, ADR-0001) and later steps read labels from that
  in-memory configuration. This settles the open point in spec §7.3 ("Whether it is stored or
  refetched is a persistence ADR detail"): refetched.
- **Never written to storage**: payment data (US-03), if the simulated payment asks for any. It
  lives only in the payment component's memory.
- No cookies, no `localStorage`, no IndexedDB for wizard data.

**When it is written**

- On every change of a step 1 value, the raw editing values are written (the store writes
  synchronously after updating its signal), so a reload restores exactly what the person typed,
  valid or not. The values are revalidated when shown and on "Continuar" (US-01-Q-16); only a
  valid "Continuar" produces the §7.3 typed output.

**When it is read**

- Once, when the store is created (each full page load). The JSON is validated at the boundary:
  wrong `version`, invalid JSON, a `country` that is not an alpha-2 code, or values of an
  unexpected type → the entry is discarded and a `console.warn` without any value is logged.
- When step 1 renders with the configuration of this page load: values whose key is no longer
  configured are dropped from the state, and a `select` value whose option no longer exists is
  cleared (US-01-AC-23). The pruned state is written back.

**Scope per country (US-01-Q-02)**

- The entry holds at most **one** country. When a supported country's context is entered
  (ADR-0001, `/:country` route) and the stored `country` differs, the entry is deleted before
  step 1 renders. Visiting `/` or an unknown country does not delete it.
- `sessionStorage` is partitioned by origin and by tab (MDN: "partitioned by both origin and
  browser tabs (top-level browsing contexts)"), so two tabs with different countries have
  independent state.

**When it is cleared**

| Event | Effect | Owner |
|---|---|---|
| Tab or window closed | Browser deletes it (MDN: "Closing the tab/window ends the session and clears the data in `sessionStorage`.") | Browser |
| Another supported country's context entered | Entry deleted | US-01 (`QuoteStore`, called from the `/:country` route) |
| Successful payment | Entry deleted before the confirmation is shown; the confirmation keeps only the simulated quote number in memory | US-03 |
| Rejected payment | **Nothing** cleared: the person retries with the same data | US-03 |
| Unreadable or wrong-version entry | Entry deleted | US-01 |

**Privacy rules**

- Values are never logged (no `console.*` with values, warnings name keys only), never sent in a
  request (US-01-AC-27), never put in the URL, and never in the document title.
- The full document number is stored, because US-03 masks it **at display time**; the masked form
  is never stored separately.
- No client-side encryption: the key would live in the same JavaScript as the data, so it would
  add complexity without protecting against the realistic threat (script injection in the page).
  The protection is the tab lifetime, the clearing rules and the absence of third-party scripts.
- If `sessionStorage` is unavailable (blocked by the browser, quota exceeded), the store keeps the
  state in memory only and logs one `console.warn`; the wizard still works except across reloads.

### Consequences

- Good, because the person keeps their data across steps, browser back and a reload (D2), and
  after a rejected payment (D6).
- Good, because the data disappears with the tab, with a country switch and after payment (D3, D4).
- Good, because one entry with a version number and boundary validation makes later stories'
  additions (plan) and format changes safe.
- Bad, because the document number and birth date sit in clear text in the tab's storage while
  the tab is open, readable by any script running on the origin and by anyone using the same
  browser tab — mitigation: no third-party scripts, values never logged, cleared on payment and
  country switch; the residual risk is accepted for a quote flow without accounts.
- Bad, because MDN notes the page session "survives over page reloads and restores", so a browser
  that restores a crashed or reopened session may bring the data back — mitigation: accepted;
  the data stays on the same device and profile.
- Bad, because a tab opened from the wizard tab may start with a copy of its storage (MDN: with an
  `opener`, "the `sessionStorage` is initially a copy of the opener's") — mitigation: the app opens
  no new windows; copies are independent afterwards.
- Bad, because writing on every change stores invalid intermediate values — mitigation: they are
  revalidated on display and on "Continuar"; the AC-19 guard validates before step 2.
- Neutral: spec US-01-AC-21 ("Data survives a reload") stays as written; the "memory only"
  rewrite foreseen in the spec does not apply.

### Strongest argument against

The document number and birth date stay in clear text in the tab's storage for as long as the
tab is open, readable by any script running on the origin. MDN states that the page session
"survives over page reloads and restores", so a browser that restores a crashed or reopened
session can bring that personal data back. Option 1 (memory only) avoids all of this: nothing
personal is ever written to the device. Its only cost is that a reload loses the data.

**Why we accept it:** losing everything on a reload, which users do on mobile and after errors,
fails the reload behaviour approved for AC-21 (D2), and the AC-19 guard would send the person
back to an empty step 1. The exposure is limited: no third-party scripts, values are never
logged, the entry is cleared on payment and on country switch, and the data stays on the same
device and browser profile. The residual risk is accepted for a quote flow without accounts.

### Confirmation

- Unit tests `quote-store.spec.ts`: the raw editing values (including an in-progress invalid
  value such as `'2015.5'`) are persisted on every change, and a new store instance restores them
  exactly from `sessionStorage` (AC-21); the §7.3 typed output (AC-18) is produced only on a valid
  "Continuar", never on an invalid one; entering another country deletes the entry and the original
  country is empty afterwards (AC-22); removed keys and options are pruned (AC-23); a corrupted or
  wrong-version entry is discarded with a warning that contains no value; storage unavailable →
  memory fallback.
- E2E `us-01-country-context.spec.ts` (AC-22) and `us-01-security.spec.ts` (AC-27, no value in any
  request).
- Review checklist: only `QuoteStore` references `sessionStorage`; no `localStorage`, cookies or
  IndexedDB for wizard data; no `console.*` call receives a value; US-03 clears the entry on
  successful payment and not on a rejected one.

## Pros and Cons of the Options

### 1. In memory only

- Good, because nothing is written to the device; the strongest privacy option.
- Good, because it is the simplest to implement and test.
- Bad, because a reload, which users do on mobile and after errors, loses everything (fails the
  reload behaviour proposed in US-01-Q-15; AC-21 would be rewritten).
- Bad, because a reload on step 2 or 3 sends the person back to an empty step 1 through the AC-19
  guard.

### 2. `sessionStorage` (chosen)

- Good, because it survives reloads and is cleared by the browser when the tab closes.
- Good, because it is partitioned per tab, so different countries in different tabs do not clash.
- Bad, because personal data is in clear text while the tab is open.
- Bad, because browser session restore can bring it back.

### 3. `localStorage` with an expiry

- Good, because the person could close the tab and come back within the expiry.
- Bad, because the data outlives the tab, so on a shared computer the next person can see it; the
  expiry is only enforced when the app runs again.
- Bad, because `localStorage` is shared by all tabs of the origin: a CO tab and a CL tab would
  overwrite each other's state.

### 4. Hybrid (sensitive values in memory only)

- Good, because the document number and birth date never touch storage.
- Bad, because after a reload the person must re-enter exactly the most tedious fields, and the
  AC-19 guard sends them back to step 1 with a partially filled form; AC-21 would hold only for
  some fields.
- Bad, because which keys are sensitive is decided in code, while editors can add new fields
  (for example a phone number) that would silently be stored.

## More Information

- MDN Web Docs, `Window.sessionStorage`
  (https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Window/sessionStorage), read on 2026-11-20:
  lifetime ("survives over page reloads and restores"; "Closing the tab/window ends the session
  and clears the data"), partitioning by origin and tab, copy from an opener.
- Related ADRs: ADR-0001 (country context and the `/:country` route that triggers the switch),
  ADR-0002 (step 1 values never sent; AC-27), ADR-0004 (forms library, reserved: how the form is
  hydrated from the store).
- Revisit when: the product needs to resume a quote on another day or device (that needs a
  server, out of scope), or real personal data is processed (a privacy review would then be
  required).
- Clarified at HC2 (Felipe Sabogal, 2026-11-20): raw editing values in storage; §7.3 typed output
  only on a valid Continuar.

8	
9	# ADR-0002: Strapi access and security model
10	
11	## Context and Problem Statement
12	
13	The browser must read published content (countries and form fields in US-01, plans in US-02,
14	terms in US-03) from Strapi, and nothing else. We must decide how the browser reaches Strapi
15	(directly or through a proxy, anonymously or with a token), how the same build learns the API
16	address in every environment, how we avoid caches that would hide a newly published change, and
17	how the AC-03 end-to-end test creates content without a write credential ever reaching the
18	browser (US-01-Q-23). Inputs: US-01-AC-27, US-01-AC-03, US-01-AC-13, US-01-BR-06, US-01-Q-16.
19	
20	## Decision Drivers
21	
22	- D1. "No Strapi token with write permissions may reach the browser. Public role permissions minimal and justified" (source: Assessment, security; CLAUDE.md §3). Evaluated as "token and permission security" (source: Assessment, evaluation).
23	- D2. "The same application and the same build serve Colombia and Chile." (source: Assessment; US-01-BR-07). The build must not embed an environment-specific API address.
24	- D3. "Changing a form field or a plan in Strapi must be reflected in the app without changing code." (source: Assessment); visible on the next full page load, no cache delaying it (US-01-BR-06, US-01-Q-16).
25	- D4. "The whole project starts with a single command (for example docker compose up), with seed data for both countries" (source: Assessment, environment). Nothing may require a manual admin step to make the app work.
26	- D5. Drafts are never visible to end users (US-01-BR-06, US-01-AC-13).
27	- D6. AC-03 is automated: a test publishes a field during the run (US-01-Q-23), and the browser sees only GET requests without write tokens (US-01-AC-27).
28	- D7. Business editors use the Strapi admin, which must stay reachable (Assessment, business context).
29	
30	## Considered Options
31	
32	1. **Direct access with the public role**: the browser calls Strapi cross-origin with no token;
33	   the public role has `find`/`findOne` on the read types; the API URL comes from a runtime
34	   `config.json`.
35	2. **Same-origin nginx proxy + public role**: the nginx container that serves the Angular build
36	   forwards `GET /api/<allow-listed types>` to Strapi; the browser calls the relative path `/api`;
37	   Strapi's public role has only `find` on the read types and Strapi itself forces published
38	   content for anonymous requests.
39	3. **Same-origin nginx proxy injecting a read-only API token**: the public role has no content
40	   permissions; nginx adds `Authorization: Bearer <read token>` to proxied requests; the token
41	   lives only in the proxy's environment.
42	
43	## Decision Outcome
44	
45	Chosen option: **"2. Same-origin nginx proxy + public role"**, because it meets D1 with no token
46	anywhere near the browser and no secret to provision at start-up (D4), gives the same build a
47	relative API address that works in every environment (D2), and places the cache and method rules
48	in one small config file (D3, D6). The extra safeguard that matters most, forcing published
49	content, is enforced **inside Strapi**, so it holds even for requests that bypass the proxy (D5,
50	D7).
51	
52	### What is decided
53	
54	**Topology (docker compose)**
55	
56	- `frontend`: nginx (Docker Official Image) serving the Angular build on one origin, and proxying
57	  `/api/` to Strapi. The upstream address comes from an environment variable through the image's
58	  template mechanism (`/etc/nginx/templates/*.template` processed with `envsubst` into
59	  `/etc/nginx/conf.d` at container start; Docker Official Image "nginx" docs). The browser bundle
60	  contains no host name.
61	- `strapi`: exposes its own port for the admin panel used by editors (D7). The content API on that
62	  port is protected by the Strapi-side rules below, not by the proxy.
63	- Development (`ng serve`) uses the Angular dev-server proxy for `/api`, so the code path is the
64	  same relative URL. No `environment.ts` API URL, no runtime `config.json` (nothing to configure).
65	
66	**Proxy rules (nginx)**
67	
68	- Only `GET` (and the implicit `HEAD`) on an allow-list of paths: `/api/countries` and
69	  `/api/form-fields` in US-01; US-02 and US-03 add `/api/plans` and `/api/terms` through their
70	  specs. Any other method or path under `/api/` returns `405` or `404` without reaching Strapi.
71	- Responses under `/api/` carry `Cache-Control: no-store`; no `proxy_cache` is configured.
72	  `index.html` is served with `Cache-Control: no-cache`; hashed build assets may be cached long-term
73	  (their names change on every build).
74	- Requests carrying an `Authorization` header are rejected (`400`), so the proxy can never be used
75	  to replay a token from a browser.
76	
77	**Strapi rules (bootstrap code, idempotent, applied on every start; no manual admin clicks)**
78	
79	- Public role: **exactly** `api::country.country.find` and `api::form-field.form-field.find` in
80	  US-01 (US-02 adds `api::plan.plan.find`, US-03 `api::terms.terms.find`). No `findOne`: the app
81	  never reads a single document by `documentId`. Justification per permission is in the table
82	  below. Bootstrap reconciles the role to this list (removes anything else) on every start.
83	- The users-permissions defaults on the public role (`auth.callback`, `auth.connect`,
84	  `auth.forgotPassword`, `auth.resetPassword`, `auth.register`, `auth.emailConfirmation`,
85	  `auth.sendEmailConfirmation`, `auth.refresh`) are removed, and the advanced setting
86	  `allow_register` is set to `false`. Verified in `@strapi/plugin-users-permissions@5.63.0`:
87	  `services/users-permissions.js` (`DEFAULT_PERMISSIONS`) and `bootstrap/index.js`
88	  (`allow_register: true` by default). The app has no end-user accounts, so these endpoints are
89	  unneeded attack surface. Note: the plugin recreates its defaults only when the permissions table
90	  is empty (`syncPermissions`), which never happens while our `find` permissions exist.
91	- The authenticated role gets no content permissions.
92	- **Published only for anonymous reads.** The REST API accepts `status=draft` from any caller
93	  that has `find` (verified: `@strapi/utils@5.63.0` `content-api-constants.js` lists `status` as an
94	  allowed query parameter; `@strapi/core@5.63.0` `core-api/service/core-service.js` defaults it to
95	  `published` only when absent; the Strapi REST docs page on `status` states no permission
96	  requirement for `status=draft`). With a plain public `find`, anyone could read drafts with
97	  `?status=draft`. A Strapi global middleware therefore removes `status`, `publicationFilter` and
98	  `hasPublishedVersion` from content API requests that are not authenticated by an API token, so
99	  the default (`published`) always applies to anonymous reads.
100	- CORS (`strapi::cors`, default `origin: '*'` in `@strapi/core@5.63.0` `middlewares/cors.js`) is
101	  restricted to an environment-driven allow-list, empty by default: the browser reaches the
102	  content API same-origin through nginx and never needs CORS.
103	- Strapi creates a default "Full Access" API token on a fresh database with no admin user and no
104	  token (`@strapi/admin@5.63.0` `bootstrap.js`, `createDefaultAPITokensIfNeeded`). It never
105	  reaches the browser, but it is an unused write credential: bootstrap deletes the default
106	  "Full Access" token, and it is never copied into any `.env`.
107	
108	| Public permission | Why it is needed | Data exposed |
109	|---|---|---|
110	| `api::country.country.find` | Chooser, unknown-country links, currency and locale (ADR-0001); required by Strapi to filter `form-field` by `country.code` | Country code, name, currency, locale. Public by nature. |
111	| `api::form-field.form-field.find` | Step 1 form (US-01-BR-01) | Labels, rules, options, Spanish copy. Public by nature (shown to every visitor). |
112	
113	**Caching**
114	
115	- No HTTP cache interceptor and no service worker caching of `/api/` in Angular; content is loaded
116	  once per full page load and held in memory (US-01-Q-16, ADR-0001).
117	- No Strapi REST cache plugin. Strapi 5.63.0 core sets no `Cache-Control` on content API
118	  responses (no occurrence in `@strapi/core@5.63.0/dist`); nginx adds `no-store`.
119	
120	**End-to-end writes for AC-03 (US-01-Q-23)**
121	
122	- The write credential exists only in the **Playwright Node process**. Flow:
123	  1. Bootstrap creates a development super admin from `STRAPI_ADMIN_EMAIL` /
124	     `STRAPI_ADMIN_PASSWORD` when no admin user exists (fictitious values in `.env.example`; real
125	     `.env` git-ignored). The human uses the same account at HC3.
126	  2. The test's setup logs in to the admin API (`POST /admin/login`, verified in
127	     `@strapi/admin@5.63.0` `routes/authentication.js`; the response includes an access token)
128	     directly against Strapi's port, not through nginx.
129	  3. It creates a **custom** API token (`POST /admin/api-tokens`, type `custom`, verified in
130	     `routes/api-tokens.js` and `services/constants.js`: types `read-only`, `full-access`,
131	     `custom`) scoped to `api::form-field.form-field.create` and `.delete`, with the shortest
132	     lifespan Strapi accepts (7 days; the validator accepts only `null`, 7, 30 or 90 days).
133	  4. It creates the `mobilePhone` field with `POST /api/form-fields` on Strapi's port. A REST
134	     `POST` publishes immediately unless `status=draft` is passed (Strapi REST docs, `status`
135	     page), which is what AC-03 needs.
136	  5. Teardown deletes the field and then the token (`DELETE /admin/api-tokens/:id`), also when the
137	     test fails.
138	- The token and the admin JWT are never passed to `page.evaluate`, `page.route`,
139	  `addInitScript`, cookies or storage of the browser context. The browser under test talks only to
140	  nginx, which rejects any `Authorization` header and any non-GET method.
141	
142	### Consequences
143	
144	- Good, because no token of any kind is ever sent by the browser or stored on disk by the app (D1).
145	- Good, because the same build runs in compose, in `ng serve` and in any future host: the API path
146	  is relative (D2).
147	- Good, because drafts stay unreadable even when someone calls Strapi's port directly with
148	  `?status=draft` (D5).
149	- Good, because one start command is enough: no token has to be generated and copied before the
150	  front end works (D4).
151	- Bad, because anyone who can reach Strapi's port can call the two public `find` endpoints
152	  directly, bypassing the proxy's allow-list — mitigation: the data is public by nature, drafts are
153	  blocked in Strapi, and the role has no other permission. Rate limiting is out of scope.
154	- Bad, because the published-only rule is custom middleware that a Strapi upgrade could make
155	  incomplete (for example a new publication query parameter) — mitigation: an automated check
156	  (below) requests the seeded draft field anonymously; re-verify on every Strapi upgrade.
157	- Bad, because the e2e setup depends on Strapi's admin API (`/admin/login`, `/admin/api-tokens`),
158	  which is what the admin panel uses but is less documented than the REST API — mitigation: it is
159	  used only by tests; if it changes, only the AC-03 test breaks, and the HC3 manual check of AC-03
160	  in the admin remains.
161	- Bad, because a development admin account is created from environment variables — mitigation:
162	  fictitious values only in `.env.example`, `.env` git-ignored, and `scripts/scan-secrets.sh`.
163	- Neutral: nginx is needed anyway to serve the Angular build; the proxy adds a few lines of
164	  configuration, not a new service.
165	
166	### Strongest argument against
167	
168	Strapi's own port, which stays open for the admin panel, still answers the public `find`
169	endpoints to anyone who can reach it, and those requests skip the proxy's method and path
170	allow-list entirely. On that port, keeping drafts hidden rests only on custom published-only
171	middleware, which a Strapi upgrade could quietly make incomplete (for example through a new
172	publication query parameter) without any error. Option 3 (proxy-injected read-only token, empty
173	public role) would close Strapi's port to anonymous content reads altogether.
174	
175	**Why we accept it:** the two exposed endpoints serve data that is public by nature, and the
176	public role has no other permission. Option 3 needs the token to exist before nginx starts,
177	which breaks the single start command (D4), and it gives the browser the same effective access
178	through the proxy, so its gain is limited to the direct port. The draft rule is guarded by an
179	automated anonymous request for the seeded draft field, re-run on every Strapi upgrade.
180	
181	### Confirmation
182	
183	- E2E `us-01-security.spec.ts` (AC-27): every browser request to `/api/` is a `GET`, none has an
184	  `Authorization` header, none contains a step 1 value.
185	- Check in the same file (an API request from the Node process, no browser): anonymous
186	  `GET /api/form-fields?status=draft&filters[key][$eq]=email` on Strapi's port returns no `email`
187	  field; `POST /api/form-fields` through nginx returns `405`.
188	- E2E `us-01-config-change.spec.ts` (AC-03) follows the write flow above; review checks that the
189	  token is created and deleted in Node only.
190	- Review checklist: bootstrap reconciles the public role to the table above; `allow_register` is
191	  `false`; no `Authorization` header and no Strapi host name in `frontend/src`;
192	  `scripts/scan-secrets.sh` exits 0.
193	
194	## Pros and Cons of the Options
195	
196	### 1. Direct access with the public role
197	
198	- Good, because there is no proxy configuration at all.
199	- Bad, because the browser needs Strapi's absolute address, so the build needs a runtime
200	  `config.json` fetched before bootstrap (`provideAppInitializer`, present in
201	  `@angular/core@22.3.0`), a second artefact per environment.
202	- Bad, because Strapi's CORS (default `origin: '*'`) must be opened to the front-end origin.
203	- Bad, because caching and method rules can only live in Strapi.
204	
205	### 2. Same-origin nginx proxy + public role (chosen)
206	
207	- Good, because no token exists in the read path; nothing to provision.
208	- Good, because the API address is relative; CORS can be closed.
209	- Good, because method, path and cache rules sit in one reviewed file.
210	- Bad, because Strapi's own port still answers the public `find` endpoints (mitigated as above).
211	
212	### 3. Same-origin nginx proxy injecting a read-only API token
213	
214	- Good, because the public role can be empty: Strapi's port answers `403` to anonymous content
215	  requests.
216	- Bad, because the token must exist before nginx starts: Strapi generates the key randomly at
217	  creation (`@strapi/admin@5.63.0` `services/api-token.js`, `crypto.randomBytes`), so a single
218	  `docker compose up` would need Strapi to write the secret to a shared volume or to insert a
219	  pre-hashed key using its internal hashing, both fragile (D4).
220	- Bad, because the `read-only` type grants `find`/`findOne` on **every** content type, including
221	  future ones, and `status=draft` is still accepted; a `custom` token narrows it, but the
222	  published-only rule is still needed.
223	- Bad, because the proxy then grants anyone who reaches it the token's rights, so the browser's
224	  effective access is the same as option 2: the security gain is only on Strapi's direct port.
225	
226	## More Information
227	
228	- Verified sources (2026-11-20; packages fetched with `npm pack` into a temporary directory):
229	  `@strapi/core@5.63.0`, `@strapi/utils@5.63.0`, `@strapi/admin@5.63.0`,
230	  `@strapi/plugin-users-permissions@5.63.0`, `@angular/core@22.3.0` (files cited inline);
231	  https://docs.strapi.io/cms/api/rest/status (REST default `published`, `POST`/`PUT` publish
232	  unless `status=draft`); https://hub.docker.com/_/nginx (environment variables via templates).
233	- Related ADRs: ADR-0001 (which types are per country, and why `country` must be readable),
234	  ADR-0003 (step 1 values never leave the browser).
235	- Revisit when: the app gains end-user accounts, content that is not public appears, Strapi's
236	  port must be reachable from the internet without the proxy, or Strapi adds a permission for
237	  reading drafts through the content API.

8	
9	# ADR-0003: Front-end persistence of the wizard state
10	
11	## Context and Problem Statement
12	
13	The wizard keeps the step 1 values (US-01), later the chosen plan (US-02), between steps and must
14	not send them to any server. The person must find their data when going back (US-01-AC-04,
15	US-01-AC-20) and, after a rejected payment, "try again without losing my information" (US-03
16	story). The values include personal data: the document number and the birth date. We must decide
17	where the state lives, what is stored, how it is scoped per country, and when it is cleared
18	(US-01-Q-15, answered "decided by the ADR; sessionStorage is the starting point", and
19	US-01-Q-02, default accepted).
20	
21	## Decision Drivers
22	
23	- D1. "Use a front-end strategy to persist the data; a database is not required." (source: Assessment; US-01-BR-08)
24	- D2. Data kept when going back, in-app and with browser back (US-01-AC-04, US-01-AC-20) and across a reload in the same tab, proposed by US-01-Q-15 (US-01-AC-21).
25	- D3. Data never crosses countries; opening another country's context discards the previous one (US-01-BR-07, US-01-AC-22, US-01-Q-02).
26	- D4. Privacy: document number and birth date are personal data (US-01-Q-15; spec §9 security/privacy). Step 1 values are never sent to a server or written to logs (US-01-AC-27, CLAUDE.md §3). Masking in the summary (US-03 story: "The document number is shown partially masked").
27	- D5. A changed configuration must not resurrect values of removed fields or options (US-01-Q-16, US-01-AC-23).
28	- D6. Retry after a failed payment keeps the data; a successful payment ends the quote (US-03 story: "Rejected payment", "Successful payment").
29	- D7. "Use fictitious data only." (source: Assessment). Tests and fixtures use only seed values.
30	
31	## Considered Options
32	
33	1. **In memory only** (a signal store, lost on reload).
34	2. **`sessionStorage`**, one versioned entry, scoped to one country, cleared on country change,
35	   tab close and successful payment.
36	3. **`localStorage` with an expiry** (for example 30 minutes), same shape.
37	4. **Hybrid**: `sessionStorage` for non-sensitive values, document number and birth date in
38	   memory only.
39	
40	## Decision Outcome
41	
42	Chosen option: **"2. sessionStorage"**, because it is the only option that survives a reload in
43	the same tab (D2) while being deleted by the browser when the tab closes, and its per-tab
44	partitioning keeps a CO tab and a CL tab from overwriting each other (D3). The privacy cost
45	(personal data in clear text in the tab's storage) is bounded by the tab lifetime and the
46	clearing rules below (D4).
47	
48	### What is decided
49	
50	**Store and storage key**
51	
52	- A root-provided `QuoteStore` (signals) is the single owner of the wizard state. Components and
53	  guards never touch `sessionStorage` directly.
54	- One `sessionStorage` entry, key `quote-wizard`, value JSON:
55	  `{ "version": 1, "country": "<code>", "step1": { "values": { "<key>": <value> } }, "plan": … }`.
56	  `values` holds the **raw editing values** of the form model: strings for `text`, `number`,
57	  `select` and `date`, booleans for `checkbox`, and `''` for an empty field. An in-progress
58	  invalid value such as `'2015.5'` is stored as typed. The spec §7.3 typed output (`text` →
59	  trimmed string, `number` → integer, `select` → option value, `date` → `YYYY-MM-DD`, `checkbox`
60	  → boolean, unchecked optional checkbox → `false`, empty optional → `null`) is produced only on a
61	  valid "Continuar"; that typed output is what US-02 and US-03 consume. `plan` is added by US-02
62	  (an identifier of the chosen plan only, defined in its spec).
63	- **Not stored**: the field configuration, labels, option labels, plans, prices or terms. They are
64	  fetched once per full page load (US-01-Q-16, ADR-0001) and later steps read labels from that
65	  in-memory configuration. This settles the open point in spec §7.3 ("Whether it is stored or
66	  refetched is a persistence ADR detail"): refetched.
67	- **Never written to storage**: payment data (US-03), if the simulated payment asks for any. It
68	  lives only in the payment component's memory.
69	- No cookies, no `localStorage`, no IndexedDB for wizard data.
70	
71	**When it is written**
72	
73	- On every change of a step 1 value, the raw editing values are written (the store writes
74	  synchronously after updating its signal), so a reload restores exactly what the person typed,
75	  valid or not. The values are revalidated when shown and on "Continuar" (US-01-Q-16); only a
76	  valid "Continuar" produces the §7.3 typed output.
77	
78	**When it is read**
79	
80	- Once, when the store is created (each full page load). The JSON is validated at the boundary:
81	  wrong `version`, invalid JSON, a `country` that is not an alpha-2 code, or values of an
82	  unexpected type → the entry is discarded and a `console.warn` without any value is logged.
83	- When step 1 renders with the configuration of this page load: values whose key is no longer
84	  configured are dropped from the state, and a `select` value whose option no longer exists is
85	  cleared (US-01-AC-23). The pruned state is written back.
86	
87	**Scope per country (US-01-Q-02)**
88	
89	- The entry holds at most **one** country. When a supported country's context is entered
90	  (ADR-0001, `/:country` route) and the stored `country` differs, the entry is deleted before
91	  step 1 renders. Visiting `/` or an unknown country does not delete it.
92	- `sessionStorage` is partitioned by origin and by tab (MDN: "partitioned by both origin and
93	  browser tabs (top-level browsing contexts)"), so two tabs with different countries have
94	  independent state.
95	
96	**When it is cleared**
97	
98	| Event | Effect | Owner |
99	|---|---|---|
100	| Tab or window closed | Browser deletes it (MDN: "Closing the tab/window ends the session and clears the data in `sessionStorage`.") | Browser |
101	| Another supported country's context entered | Entry deleted | US-01 (`QuoteStore`, called from the `/:country` route) |
102	| Successful payment | Entry deleted before the confirmation is shown; the confirmation keeps only the simulated quote number in memory | US-03 |
103	| Rejected payment | **Nothing** cleared: the person retries with the same data | US-03 |
104	| Unreadable or wrong-version entry | Entry deleted | US-01 |
105	
106	**Privacy rules**
107	
108	- Values are never logged (no `console.*` with values, warnings name keys only), never sent in a
109	  request (US-01-AC-27), never put in the URL, and never in the document title.
110	- The full document number is stored, because US-03 masks it **at display time**; the masked form
111	  is never stored separately.
112	- No client-side encryption: the key would live in the same JavaScript as the data, so it would
113	  add complexity without protecting against the realistic threat (script injection in the page).
114	  The protection is the tab lifetime, the clearing rules and the absence of third-party scripts.
115	- If `sessionStorage` is unavailable (blocked by the browser, quota exceeded), the store keeps the
116	  state in memory only and logs one `console.warn`; the wizard still works except across reloads.
117	
118	### Consequences
119	
120	- Good, because the person keeps their data across steps, browser back and a reload (D2), and
121	  after a rejected payment (D6).
122	- Good, because the data disappears with the tab, with a country switch and after payment (D3, D4).
123	- Good, because one entry with a version number and boundary validation makes later stories'
124	  additions (plan) and format changes safe.
125	- Bad, because the document number and birth date sit in clear text in the tab's storage while
126	  the tab is open, readable by any script running on the origin and by anyone using the same
127	  browser tab — mitigation: no third-party scripts, values never logged, cleared on payment and
128	  country switch; the residual risk is accepted for a quote flow without accounts.
129	- Bad, because MDN notes the page session "survives over page reloads and restores", so a browser
130	  that restores a crashed or reopened session may bring the data back — mitigation: accepted;
131	  the data stays on the same device and profile.
132	- Bad, because a tab opened from the wizard tab may start with a copy of its storage (MDN: with an
133	  `opener`, "the `sessionStorage` is initially a copy of the opener's") — mitigation: the app opens
134	  no new windows; copies are independent afterwards.
135	- Bad, because writing on every change stores invalid intermediate values — mitigation: they are
136	  revalidated on display and on "Continuar"; the AC-19 guard validates before step 2.
137	- Neutral: spec US-01-AC-21 ("Data survives a reload") stays as written; the "memory only"
138	  rewrite foreseen in the spec does not apply.
139	
140	### Strongest argument against
141	
142	The document number and birth date stay in clear text in the tab's storage for as long as the
143	tab is open, readable by any script running on the origin. MDN states that the page session
144	"survives over page reloads and restores", so a browser that restores a crashed or reopened
145	session can bring that personal data back. Option 1 (memory only) avoids all of this: nothing
146	personal is ever written to the device. Its only cost is that a reload loses the data.
147	
148	**Why we accept it:** losing everything on a reload, which users do on mobile and after errors,
149	fails the reload behaviour approved for AC-21 (D2), and the AC-19 guard would send the person
150	back to an empty step 1. The exposure is limited: no third-party scripts, values are never
151	logged, the entry is cleared on payment and on country switch, and the data stays on the same
152	device and browser profile. The residual risk is accepted for a quote flow without accounts.
153	
154	### Confirmation
155	
156	- Unit tests `quote-store.spec.ts`: the raw editing values (including an in-progress invalid
157	  value such as `'2015.5'`) are persisted on every change, and a new store instance restores them
158	  exactly from `sessionStorage` (AC-21); the §7.3 typed output (AC-18) is produced only on a valid
159	  "Continuar", never on an invalid one; entering another country deletes the entry and the original
160	  country is empty afterwards (AC-22); removed keys and options are pruned (AC-23); a corrupted or
161	  wrong-version entry is discarded with a warning that contains no value; storage unavailable →
162	  memory fallback.
163	- E2E `us-01-country-context.spec.ts` (AC-22) and `us-01-security.spec.ts` (AC-27, no value in any
164	  request).
165	- Review checklist: only `QuoteStore` references `sessionStorage`; no `localStorage`, cookies or
166	  IndexedDB for wizard data; no `console.*` call receives a value; US-03 clears the entry on
167	  successful payment and not on a rejected one.
168	
169	## Pros and Cons of the Options
170	
171	### 1. In memory only
172	
173	- Good, because nothing is written to the device; the strongest privacy option.
174	- Good, because it is the simplest to implement and test.
175	- Bad, because a reload, which users do on mobile and after errors, loses everything (fails the
176	  reload behaviour proposed in US-01-Q-15; AC-21 would be rewritten).
177	- Bad, because a reload on step 2 or 3 sends the person back to an empty step 1 through the AC-19
178	  guard.
179	
180	### 2. `sessionStorage` (chosen)
181	
182	- Good, because it survives reloads and is cleared by the browser when the tab closes.
183	- Good, because it is partitioned per tab, so different countries in different tabs do not clash.
184	- Bad, because personal data is in clear text while the tab is open.
185	- Bad, because browser session restore can bring it back.
186	
187	### 3. `localStorage` with an expiry
188	
189	- Good, because the person could close the tab and come back within the expiry.
190	- Bad, because the data outlives the tab, so on a shared computer the next person can see it; the
191	  expiry is only enforced when the app runs again.
192	- Bad, because `localStorage` is shared by all tabs of the origin: a CO tab and a CL tab would
193	  overwrite each other's state.
194	
195	### 4. Hybrid (sensitive values in memory only)
196	
197	- Good, because the document number and birth date never touch storage.
198	- Bad, because after a reload the person must re-enter exactly the most tedious fields, and the
199	  AC-19 guard sends them back to step 1 with a partially filled form; AC-21 would hold only for
200	  some fields.
201	- Bad, because which keys are sensitive is decided in code, while editors can add new fields
202	  (for example a phone number) that would silently be stored.
203	
204	## More Information
205	
206	- MDN Web Docs, `Window.sessionStorage`
207	  (https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Window/sessionStorage), read on 2026-11-20:
208	  lifetime ("survives over page reloads and restores"; "Closing the tab/window ends the session
209	  and clears the data"), partitioning by origin and tab, copy from an opener.
210	- Related ADRs: ADR-0001 (country context and the `/:country` route that triggers the switch),
211	  ADR-0002 (step 1 values never sent; AC-27), ADR-0004 (forms library, reserved: how the form is
212	  hydrated from the store).
213	- Revisit when: the product needs to resume a quote on another day or device (that needs a
214	  server, out of scope), or real personal data is processed (a privacy review would then be
215	  required).
216	- Clarified at HC2 (Felipe Sabogal, 2026-11-20): raw editing values in storage; §7.3 typed output
217	  only on a valid Continuar.

9	# ADR-0006: Strapi physical model adjustments: typed validation-rule parameters and the country `localeTag` attribute (amends ADR-0001)
10	
11	## Context and Problem Statement
12	
13	ADR-0001 (Accepted) fixes the Strapi model for US-01. Code review round 1 found two places where
14	the implementation departs from it, or from spec §7.1, without a recorded decision:
15	
16	1. **Rule parameters (US-01-R1-F04).** `form.validation-rule` stores the parameter of
17	   `minLength`, `maxLength`, `min`, `max` and `pattern` in a free `json` attribute `value`
18	   (`backend/src/components/form/validation-rule.json`). Spec §7.1 says the rule kinds are
19	   "structured, not free JSON". Editors must type JSON (a regex needs quotes and doubled
20	   backslashes), and a value of the wrong type saves without error and then makes the front-end
21	   boundary parser drop the **whole field** (`frontend/src/app/shared/field-config.ts`), so a
22	   required reserved field such as `plate` can silently disappear from the form.
23	2. **Country locale (US-01-R1-F05).** ADR-0001 names the BCP 47 attribute of `country` `locale`.
24	   `locale` is a reserved attribute name in Strapi 5 (verified below), so commit 241340a stores
25	   it as `localeTag` and adds a custom `find` controller
26	   (`backend/src/api/country/controllers/country.ts`) that renames it back to `locale`, but only
27	   for `fields`. `sort=locale:asc` and `filters[locale][$eq]=es-CO` return
28	   `400 Invalid key locale` (reproduced by the reviewer). US-02 will consume this attribute for
29	   currency and number formatting.
30	
31	The human (Felipe Sabogal, 2026-11-21) decided the direction of both points after the review.
32	This ADR records the options and the decision. It amends **only** these two points of
33	ADR-0001's "What is decided → Strapi model"; everything else in ADR-0001 stays as written.
34	Story: US-01 (`specs/US-01/spec.md` §7.1, §7.3).
35	
36	## Decision Drivers
37	
38	- D1. "The business team, which is not technical, must be able to change the form fields and the offered plans from Strapi without requesting a deployment." (source: Assessment, business context; US-01-BR-06). An editor must be able to enter a rule parameter without knowing JSON syntax or escaping.
39	- D2. Rule kinds are "structured, not free JSON" (source: spec §7.1); "Editors must not be able to save something the frontend cannot parse" (source: `strapi-content-modeling` skill, modeling conventions).
40	- D3. A malformed configuration is not rendered and the app keeps working (source: US-01-Q-18, US-01-AC-14). The boundary parser stays the last line of defence, whatever the schema.
41	- D4. Keep bespoke backend code to a minimum: each custom controller or middleware must be reviewed and re-verified on every Strapi upgrade (source: human decision, Felipe Sabogal, 2026-11-21, the same reasoning recorded as D3 in ADR-0005).
42	- D5. The country attribute that carries the number locale must be fully usable through the stock content API: `fields`, `sort` and `filters` (source: US-01-R1-F05; US-02 story, "The price is shown in the country's currency and format").
43	- D6. Decisions are recorded and accepted ADRs are not rewritten (source: CLAUDE.md §1; `adr-madr` skill lifecycle).
44	
45	## Considered Options
46	
47	Point 1, rule parameters (`form.validation-rule`):
48	
49	1. **1a. Typed attributes per parameter** on the one component: numeric `value`, string
50	   `pattern`, integers `years`, `maxYearsOld`, `maxYearsAhead`; unused ones are null.
51	2. **1b. Keep the `json` `value`** and add server-side validation on save (a Document Service
52	   middleware or lifecycle that rejects a value of the wrong type for the rule `kind`).
53	3. **1c. A `string` `value`** that editors type as plain text, coerced to a number by the
54	   front-end parser for numeric kinds.
55	4. **1d. One component per rule kind in a dynamic zone** (`rules` becomes a `dynamiczone` on
56	   `form-field` with components such as `rule.min-length`, `rule.pattern`, `rule.min-age`,
57	   `rule.year-range`, `rule.rut-check-digit`, each with only its own, required, parameters).
58	
59	Point 2, country locale attribute:
60	
61	1. **2a. Expose `localeTag` as is**: the stored attribute and the API field are both
62	   `localeTag`; the front-end boundary parser maps it to its internal `locale`. The custom
63	   `find` controller is removed.
64	2. **2b. Keep the renaming controller and complete it**: also translate `sort` and `filters`
65	   (and any nested form of them) from `locale` to `localeTag`.
66	3. **2c. Another attribute name** chosen for readability (for example `numberLocale` or
67	   `formatLocale`), exposed as is.
68	
69	## Decision Outcome
70	
71	Chosen options: **"1a. Typed attributes per parameter"** and **"2a. Expose `localeTag` as is"**.
72	
73	1a, because each parameter gets a Strapi type the admin enforces on save (a number field cannot
74	hold `"tres"`, a regex is typed as plain text with no escaping), which meets D1 and D2 with a
75	one-file schema change and no custom backend code (D4), while keeping one repeatable component
76	and the current `rules` shape that the front end, seed and tests already use. 2a, because it uses
77	the stock controller, so `fields`, `sort` and `filters` all work (D5), and it removes custom code
78	instead of extending it (D4).
79	
80	### What is decided (amendment to ADR-0001, "What is decided → Strapi model")
81	
82	**`form.validation-rule` component** (`backend/src/components/form/validation-rule.json`):
83	
84	| Attribute | Strapi type | Used by kind | Notes |
85	|---|---|---|---|
86	| `kind` | `enumeration` (unchanged) | all | Required. `minLength`, `maxLength`, `min`, `max`, `pattern`, `minAge`, `yearRange`, `rutCheckDigit`. |
87	| `value` | `decimal` (replaces `json`) | `minLength`, `maxLength`, `min`, `max` | Numeric. Integer ≥ 0 for `minLength`/`maxLength` (checked at the boundary). |
88	| `pattern` | `string` (new) | `pattern` | ECMAScript regex source, no flags, typed as plain text. |
89	| `years` | `integer`, `min: 1` (unchanged) | `minAge` | |
90	| `maxYearsOld` | `integer`, `min: 0` (unchanged) | `yearRange` | |
91	| `maxYearsAhead` | `integer`, `min: 0` (unchanged) | `yearRange` | |
92	| `message` | `string` (unchanged) | all | Optional rule-specific message. |
93	
94	- Parameters a kind does not use are left empty and arrive as `null`. Strapi cannot make an
95	  attribute required depending on `kind`, so the front-end boundary parser still checks that the
96	  kind's own parameter is present and in range. The rule semantics of spec §7.1 do not change;
97	  only where the `pattern` parameter lives changes (`pattern` instead of `value`). The exact
98	  wire shape, and how a non-null unused parameter is treated, are fixed in spec v0.4.
99	- The seed (`backend/src/seed/form-fields.ts`), the annex `specs/US-01/seed-fields.md`, the
100	  front-end parser and its fixtures, and the AC-03 e2e payload move the regex from `value` to
101	  `pattern`.
102	- `decimal` was chosen over `float` because both are read back as a JavaScript number
103	  (`@strapi/database@5.63.0` `dist/fields/index.js:26-27` maps `float` and `decimal` to
104	  `NumberField`, whose `fromDB` returns `_.toNumber(value)`; `dist/query/helpers/transform.js:21`
105	  keeps `null` as `null`), and `decimal` stores values such as `0.1` exactly in the database.
106	
107	**`country` content type** (`backend/src/api/country/content-types/country/schema.json`):
108	
109	- The BCP 47 attribute is named **`localeTag`** (string, required), in storage and on the wire.
110	  ADR-0001's `locale` is replaced by `localeTag` everywhere it refers to the Strapi attribute
111	  (the model list, and the "narrow `fields[]`" request of the chooser, which asks for
112	  `localeTag`).
113	- `backend/src/api/country/controllers/country.ts` goes back to
114	  `factories.createCoreController('api::country.country')`.
115	- The front-end boundary parser (`frontend/src/app/shared/country.ts`) reads `localeTag` from the
116	  response and maps it to the internal `Country.locale` (or another internal name the spec
117	  chooses). Validation of the value is unchanged.
118	- ADR-0002's public role table still holds: `api::country.country.find` exposes "country code,
119	  name, currency, locale", and the locale is now carried by `localeTag`.
120	
121	### Consequences
122	
123	- Good, because an editor types `3` into a number field and `^[A-Za-z]{3}[0-9]{3}$` into a text
124	  field; Strapi refuses a non-number in `value` on save (`@strapi/core@5.63.0`
125	  `dist/services/entity-validator/validators.js:329-364`: `decimal` uses `floatValidator`,
126	  `yup.number()` with a finite-number test), so the wrong-type case of F04 can no longer reach
127	  the front end (D1, D2).
128	- Good, because both points end with **less** custom backend code: the country controller is
129	  deleted and no validation middleware is added (D4).
130	- Good, because `localeTag` works with every stock query parameter (`fields`, `sort`, `filters`),
131	  so US-02 can filter or sort on it without new backend work (D5).
132	- Bad, because a rule can still be saved without the parameter its kind needs (for example
133	  `minLength` with an empty `value`, or `pattern` with an invalid regex), and the boundary
134	  parser then drops the field — mitigation: the component's admin description lists which
135	  attribute each kind uses (as today), the parser logs a warning without user data (US-01-Q-18),
136	  and spec v0.4 keeps the malformed-rule cases in AC-14. 1d would remove the missing-parameter
137	  case; see *Strongest argument against*.
138	- Bad, because the component has fields that are meaningless for most kinds, and the admin shows
139	  all of them for every rule — mitigation: per-attribute descriptions; acceptable with eight
140	  kinds.
141	- Bad, because the wire name `localeTag` differs from the conceptual name in ADR-0001 and the
142	  US-02 story ("locale") — mitigation: the rename is confined to the boundary parser; this ADR
143	  and spec v0.4 record it.
144	- Bad, because existing development databases hold rule rows with the old `json` `value` and
145	  country rows that are already correct; the idempotent seed only creates missing items, so it
146	  will not rewrite old rule rows — mitigation: development data is disposable; reset the Strapi
147	  volume (or delete the seeded fields) after the schema change, and state this in the commit.
148	- Neutral: the public and e2e permissions of ADR-0002 and ADR-0005 do not change.
149	
150	### Strongest argument against
151	
152	**Against 1a (typed attributes):** option 1d makes invalid rules impossible to save, not merely
153	less likely. With one component per kind in a dynamic zone, each component carries only its own
154	parameters, marked `required`, so the admin will not save a `minLength` rule without a length, and
155	editors never see `years` next to a regex. Option 1a keeps a "pick a kind, then guess which of
156	five fields to fill" form, in which a missing parameter still saves and still makes the field
157	vanish from step 1, the exact failure mode F04 complained about, only narrower.
158	
159	**Why we accept it:** 1d is viable in Strapi 5.63.0 only on the content type (the content-type
160	builder allows `dynamiczone` for content types but not inside components:
161	`@strapi/content-type-builder@5.63.0` `dist/server/controllers/validation/content-type.js:35-41`
162	vs `component.js:18-22`), so it replaces `rules` with a polymorphic list of eight components. Every
163	response item gains a `__component` discriminator, the populate needs the fragment syntax
164	(`populate[rules][on][...]`, validated in `@strapi/utils@5.63.0` `dist/validate/validators.js:621`),
165	the boundary parser, seed, fixtures and AC-03 payload change shape, and a new rule kind becomes a
166	new component rather than a new enum value. That is a large change to code that passed every
167	other review item, made in a fix round. 1a removes the reported wrong-type and escaping problems
168	with one schema edit, and the remaining missing-parameter case is caught at the boundary (D3).
169	If editors produce malformed rules in practice, 1d is the upgrade path (see *Revisit when*).
170	
171	**Against 2a (expose `localeTag`):** option 2b keeps the contract ADR-0001 and the US-02 story
172	were written against: the API says `locale`, the domain says `locale`, and nobody downstream
173	needs to know about a Strapi naming restriction. 2a leaks a storage workaround into the public
174	wire contract for good, and any later consumer (another front end, an export) has to learn the
175	mapping too.
176	
177	**Why we accept it:** making 2b complete means rewriting `locale` inside `sort` (string, array
178	and object forms) and inside arbitrarily nested `filters` (`$and`, `$or`, `$not`), on every
179	route that can reach `country` (including `filters[country][locale]` on `form-field`), and
180	keeping that in step with Strapi's query parser on each upgrade. It is also shadowed by Strapi's
181	own `locale` query parameter (`@strapi/utils@5.63.0` `dist/content-api-constants.js:14`). That is
182	exactly the bespoke code D4 asks us to avoid, for a cosmetic gain. The mapping in the front end is
183	one line in a parser that already exists.
184	
185	### Confirmation
186	
187	- Schema check (review checklist): `validation-rule.json` has no `json` attribute; `value` is
188	  `decimal`, `pattern` is `string`. `country/schema.json` has `localeTag` and no `locale`.
189	  `backend/src/api/country/controllers/country.ts` is the plain `createCoreController`.
190	- Runtime check (strapi-developer, recorded in the review response):
191	  `GET /api/countries?fields[0]=code&fields[1]=localeTag&sort=localeTag:asc&filters[localeTag][$eq]=es-CO`
192	  returns `200` with `localeTag: "es-CO"` and only CO.
193	- Unit tests: `country.spec.ts` (parser reads `localeTag`, drops an entry without it);
194	  `field-config.spec.ts` (a `pattern` rule reads `pattern`; a numeric rule reads a number
195	  `value`; a rule missing its kind's parameter makes the field malformed, per spec v0.4 AC-14).
196	- `grep -rn "'locale'" frontend/src/app/core` finds no `fields[...]=locale` request.
197	
198	## Pros and Cons of the Options
199	
200	### 1a. Typed attributes per parameter (chosen)
201	
202	- Good, because the admin type-checks each parameter on save, and a regex is plain text.
203	- Good, because the change is one component file; the `rules` shape (repeatable component with
204	  `kind`) stays.
205	- Good, because no backend code is added (D4).
206	- Bad, because a missing parameter still saves; the boundary parser must catch it.
207	- Bad, because every rule shows all parameter inputs in the admin.
208	
209	### 1b. Keep `json` and validate on save
210	
211	- Good, because the schema does not change, and invalid values are rejected on save with an
212	  error the editor sees.
213	- Good, because the check could also cover a missing parameter and an invalid regex.
214	- Bad, because editors still type JSON, with quotes and doubled backslashes in a regex (against
215	  D1); the core complaint of F04 stays.
216	- Bad, because it adds a custom Document Service middleware or lifecycle on the write path, to
217	  test and re-verify on each upgrade (against D4).
218	
219	### 1c. `string` `value` coerced by the front end
220	
221	- Good, because a regex is plain text and the schema change is minimal.
222	- Bad, because a number is also free text: `"tres"` or `"3,5"` still saves and the field still
223	  disappears, so the wrong-type case of F04 is not solved (against D2).
224	- Bad, because the coercion rules (comma vs dot, spaces, `"03"`) become front-end logic that
225	  editors cannot see.
226	
227	### 1d. One component per rule kind in a dynamic zone
228	
229	Viable in 5.63.0 on the `form-field` content type only: the content-type builder lists
230	`dynamiczone` in the valid types for content types
231	(`@strapi/content-type-builder@5.63.0` `dist/server/controllers/validation/content-type.js:35-41`)
232	and not for components (`component.js:18-22`). Dynamic-zone entries carry `__component`
233	(`@strapi/utils@5.63.0` `dist/content-types.js`, `DYNAMIC_ZONE_KEYS`).
234	
235	- Good, because each kind has only its own, required, typed parameters: a rule without its
236	  parameter cannot be saved.
237	- Good, because the admin shows a clear "add a rule of type X" picker.
238	- Bad, because `rules` changes from a repeatable component to a polymorphic list: new populate
239	  syntax, a `__component` discriminator in the parser, and a new seed and fixture shape.
240	- Bad, because adding a rule kind means a new component (schema plus code), not an enum value.
241	- Bad, because it is the largest change of the four, in a review-fix round.
242	
243	### 2a. Expose `localeTag` (chosen)
244	
245	- Good, because the stock controller handles `fields`, `sort` and `filters` (D5).
246	- Good, because it deletes the custom controller (D4).
247	- Bad, because the wire name differs from the domain name; the parser maps it.
248	
249	### 2b. Keep and complete the renaming controller
250	
251	- Good, because the API keeps the name `locale` from ADR-0001 and the US-02 story.
252	- Bad, because a complete rename covers `sort` and nested `filters` on every route that reaches
253	  `country`, and must track Strapi's query parsing (against D4).
254	- Bad, because `locale` is also Strapi's own query parameter, so the name stays ambiguous in the
255	  API.
256	
257	### 2c. Another attribute name (for example `numberLocale`)
258	
259	- Good, because the stock controller works, as in 2a, and the name may describe the purpose
260	  better.
261	- Bad, because the implementation, seed, fixtures and spec v0.4 already use `localeTag`; a
262	  different name is churn with no functional gain.
263	- Neutral: functionally equivalent to 2a.
264	
265	## More Information
266	
267	- **`locale` is reserved in Strapi 5.63.0** (verified in the installed packages, 5.63.0 per their
268	  `package.json`):
269	  - `@strapi/utils@5.63.0` `dist/content-types.js:51-76`, `RESERVED_ATTRIBUTE_NAMES` contains
270	    `'locale'` (line 69); `isReservedAttributeName` and `getReservedAttributeNames` use it, and
271	    the content-type builder refuses it (`@strapi/content-type-builder@5.63.0`
272	    `dist/server/services/builder.js:11`, `dist/server/controllers/validation/model-schema.js:73-85`,
273	    "Attribute keys cannot be one of …").
274	  - `@strapi/utils@5.63.0` `dist/content-api-constants.js:8-23`: `locale` is one of the shared
275	    content-API and Document Service query parameter keys.
276	  - `@strapi/core@5.63.0` `dist/services/document-service/repository.js:83-132` validates and
277	    normalises a `locale` parameter on every Document Service call, and
278	    `dist/utils/transform-content-types-to-models.js:365-372` treats a `locale` attribute as the
279	    i18n system column in the document index.
280	  - The 400 on `fields[]=locale`, `sort=locale` and `filters[locale]` with the attribute stored as
281	    `localeTag` comes from the field validator: `@strapi/utils@5.63.0`
282	    `dist/validate/validators.js:393-407` throws `Invalid key` for a key that is not a scalar
283	    attribute of the schema.
284	- Review evidence: `reviews/US-01-review-R1.md`, US-01-R1-F04 and US-01-R1-F05.
285	- Related ADRs: ADR-0001 (amended by this ADR, in the two points above only), ADR-0002 (public
286	  `country.find`, unchanged), ADR-0005 (same "less bespoke backend code" reasoning).
287	- Revisit when: editors save rules without their parameter more than occasionally (move to 1d), a
288	  rule kind needs more than one parameter of a new type, or a second consumer of the country API
289	  needs the name `locale` (then 2b, or an API version).
290
