# ADR-0006: Strapi physical model adjustments: typed validation-rule parameters and the country `localeTag` attribute (amends ADR-0001)

## Context and Problem Statement

ADR-0001 (Accepted) fixes the Strapi model for US-01. Code review round 1 found two places where
the implementation departs from it, or from spec §7.1, without a recorded decision:

1. **Rule parameters (US-01-R1-F04).** `form.validation-rule` stores the parameter of
   `minLength`, `maxLength`, `min`, `max` and `pattern` in a free `json` attribute `value`
   (`backend/src/components/form/validation-rule.json`). Spec §7.1 says the rule kinds are
   "structured, not free JSON". Editors must type JSON (a regex needs quotes and doubled
   backslashes), and a value of the wrong type saves without error and then makes the front-end
   boundary parser drop the **whole field** (`frontend/src/app/shared/field-config.ts`), so a
   required reserved field such as `plate` can silently disappear from the form.
2. **Country locale (US-01-R1-F05).** ADR-0001 names the BCP 47 attribute of `country` `locale`.
   `locale` is a reserved attribute name in Strapi 5 (verified below), so commit 241340a stores
   it as `localeTag` and adds a custom `find` controller
   (`backend/src/api/country/controllers/country.ts`) that renames it back to `locale`, but only
   for `fields`. `sort=locale:asc` and `filters[locale][$eq]=es-CO` return
   `400 Invalid key locale` (reproduced by the reviewer). US-02 will consume this attribute for
   currency and number formatting.

The human (Felipe Sabogal, 2026-11-21) decided the direction of both points after the review.
This ADR records the options and the decision. It amends **only** these two points of
ADR-0001's "What is decided → Strapi model"; everything else in ADR-0001 stays as written.
Story: US-01 (`specs/US-01/spec.md` §7.1, §7.3).

## Decision Drivers

- D1. "The business team, which is not technical, must be able to change the form fields and the offered plans from Strapi without requesting a deployment." (source: Assessment, business context; US-01-BR-06). An editor must be able to enter a rule parameter without knowing JSON syntax or escaping.
- D2. Rule kinds are "structured, not free JSON" (source: spec §7.1); "Editors must not be able to save something the frontend cannot parse" (source: `strapi-content-modeling` skill, modeling conventions).
- D3. A malformed configuration is not rendered and the app keeps working (source: US-01-Q-18, US-01-AC-14). The boundary parser stays the last line of defence, whatever the schema.
- D4. Keep bespoke backend code to a minimum: each custom controller or middleware must be reviewed and re-verified on every Strapi upgrade (source: human decision, Felipe Sabogal, 2026-11-21, the same reasoning recorded as D3 in ADR-0005).
- D5. The country attribute that carries the number locale must be fully usable through the stock content API: `fields`, `sort` and `filters` (source: US-01-R1-F05; US-02 story, "The price is shown in the country's currency and format").
- D6. Decisions are recorded and accepted ADRs are not rewritten (source: CLAUDE.md §1; `adr-madr` skill lifecycle).

## Considered Options

Point 1, rule parameters (`form.validation-rule`):

1. **1a. Typed attributes per parameter** on the one component: numeric `value`, string
   `pattern`, integers `years`, `maxYearsOld`, `maxYearsAhead`; unused ones are null.
2. **1b. Keep the `json` `value`** and add server-side validation on save (a Document Service
   middleware or lifecycle that rejects a value of the wrong type for the rule `kind`).
3. **1c. A `string` `value`** that editors type as plain text, coerced to a number by the
   front-end parser for numeric kinds.
4. **1d. One component per rule kind in a dynamic zone** (`rules` becomes a `dynamiczone` on
   `form-field` with components such as `rule.min-length`, `rule.pattern`, `rule.min-age`,
   `rule.year-range`, `rule.rut-check-digit`, each with only its own, required, parameters).

Point 2, country locale attribute:

1. **2a. Expose `localeTag` as is**: the stored attribute and the API field are both
   `localeTag`; the front-end boundary parser maps it to its internal `locale`. The custom
   `find` controller is removed.
2. **2b. Keep the renaming controller and complete it**: also translate `sort` and `filters`
   (and any nested form of them) from `locale` to `localeTag`.
3. **2c. Another attribute name** chosen for readability (for example `numberLocale` or
   `formatLocale`), exposed as is.

## Decision Outcome

Chosen options: **"1a. Typed attributes per parameter"** and **"2a. Expose `localeTag` as is"**.

1a, because each parameter gets a Strapi type the admin enforces on save (a number field cannot
hold `"tres"`, a regex is typed as plain text with no escaping), which meets D1 and D2 with a
one-file schema change and no custom backend code (D4), while keeping one repeatable component
and the current `rules` shape that the front end, seed and tests already use. 2a, because it uses
the stock controller, so `fields`, `sort` and `filters` all work (D5), and it removes custom code
instead of extending it (D4).

### What is decided (amendment to ADR-0001, "What is decided → Strapi model")

**`form.validation-rule` component** (`backend/src/components/form/validation-rule.json`):

| Attribute | Strapi type | Used by kind | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `kind` | `enumeration` (unchanged) | all | Required. `minLength`, `maxLength`, `min`, `max`, `pattern`, `minAge`, `yearRange`, `rutCheckDigit`. |
| `value` | `decimal` (replaces `json`) | `minLength`, `maxLength`, `min`, `max` | Numeric. Integer ≥ 0 for `minLength`/`maxLength` (checked at the boundary). |
| `pattern` | `string` (new) | `pattern` | ECMAScript regex source, no flags, typed as plain text. |
| `years` | `integer`, `min: 1` (unchanged) | `minAge` | |
| `maxYearsOld` | `integer`, `min: 0` (unchanged) | `yearRange` | |
| `maxYearsAhead` | `integer`, `min: 0` (unchanged) | `yearRange` | |
| `message` | `string` (unchanged) | all | Optional rule-specific message. |

- Parameters a kind does not use are left empty and arrive as `null`. Strapi cannot make an
  attribute required depending on `kind`, so the front-end boundary parser still checks that the
  kind's own parameter is present and in range. The rule semantics of spec §7.1 do not change;
  only where the `pattern` parameter lives changes (`pattern` instead of `value`). The exact
  wire shape, and how a non-null unused parameter is treated, are fixed in spec v0.4.
- The seed (`backend/src/seed/form-fields.ts`), the annex `specs/US-01/seed-fields.md`, the
  front-end parser and its fixtures, and the AC-03 e2e payload move the regex from `value` to
  `pattern`.
- `decimal` was chosen over `float` because both are read back as a JavaScript number
  (`@strapi/database@5.63.0` `dist/fields/index.js:26-27` maps `float` and `decimal` to
  `NumberField`, whose `fromDB` returns `_.toNumber(value)`; `dist/query/helpers/transform.js:21`
  keeps `null` as `null`), and `decimal` stores values such as `0.1` exactly in the database.

**`country` content type** (`backend/src/api/country/content-types/country/schema.json`):

- The BCP 47 attribute is named **`localeTag`** (string, required), in storage and on the wire.
  ADR-0001's `locale` is replaced by `localeTag` everywhere it refers to the Strapi attribute
  (the model list, and the "narrow `fields[]`" request of the chooser, which asks for
  `localeTag`).
- `backend/src/api/country/controllers/country.ts` goes back to
  `factories.createCoreController('api::country.country')`.
- The front-end boundary parser (`frontend/src/app/shared/country.ts`) reads `localeTag` from the
  response and maps it to the internal `Country.locale` (or another internal name the spec
  chooses). Validation of the value is unchanged.
- ADR-0002's public role table still holds: `api::country.country.find` exposes "country code,
  name, currency, locale", and the locale is now carried by `localeTag`.

### Consequences

- Good, because an editor types `3` into a number field and `^[A-Za-z]{3}[0-9]{3}$` into a text
  field; Strapi refuses a non-number in `value` on save (`@strapi/core@5.63.0`
  `dist/services/entity-validator/validators.js:329-364`: `decimal` uses `floatValidator`,
  `yup.number()` with a finite-number test), so the wrong-type case of F04 can no longer reach
  the front end (D1, D2).
- Good, because both points end with **less** custom backend code: the country controller is
  deleted and no validation middleware is added (D4).
- Good, because `localeTag` works with every stock query parameter (`fields`, `sort`, `filters`),
  so US-02 can filter or sort on it without new backend work (D5).
- Bad, because a rule can still be saved without the parameter its kind needs (for example
  `minLength` with an empty `value`, or `pattern` with an invalid regex), and the boundary
  parser then drops the field — mitigation: the component's admin description lists which
  attribute each kind uses (as today), the parser logs a warning without user data (US-01-Q-18),
  and spec v0.4 keeps the malformed-rule cases in AC-14. 1d would remove the missing-parameter
  case; see *Strongest argument against*.
- Bad, because the component has fields that are meaningless for most kinds, and the admin shows
  all of them for every rule — mitigation: per-attribute descriptions; acceptable with eight
  kinds.
- Bad, because the wire name `localeTag` differs from the conceptual name in ADR-0001 and the
  US-02 story ("locale") — mitigation: the rename is confined to the boundary parser; this ADR
  and spec v0.4 record it.
- Bad, because existing development databases hold rule rows with the old `json` `value` and
  country rows that are already correct; the idempotent seed only creates missing items, so it
  will not rewrite old rule rows — mitigation: development data is disposable; reset the Strapi
  volume (or delete the seeded fields) after the schema change, and state this in the commit.
- Neutral: the public and e2e permissions of ADR-0002 and ADR-0005 do not change.

### Strongest argument against

**Against 1a (typed attributes):** option 1d makes invalid rules impossible to save, not merely
less likely. With one component per kind in a dynamic zone, each component carries only its own
parameters, marked `required`, so the admin will not save a `minLength` rule without a length, and
editors never see `years` next to a regex. Option 1a keeps a "pick a kind, then guess which of
five fields to fill" form, in which a missing parameter still saves and still makes the field
vanish from step 1, the exact failure mode F04 complained about, only narrower.

**Why we accept it:** 1d is viable in Strapi 5.63.0 only on the content type (the content-type
builder allows `dynamiczone` for content types but not inside components:
`@strapi/content-type-builder@5.63.0` `dist/server/controllers/validation/content-type.js:35-41`
vs `component.js:18-22`), so it replaces `rules` with a polymorphic list of eight components. Every
response item gains a `__component` discriminator, the populate needs the fragment syntax
(`populate[rules][on][...]`, validated in `@strapi/utils@5.63.0` `dist/validate/validators.js:621`),
the boundary parser, seed, fixtures and AC-03 payload change shape, and a new rule kind becomes a
new component rather than a new enum value. That is a large change to code that passed every
other review item, made in a fix round. 1a removes the reported wrong-type and escaping problems
with one schema edit, and the remaining missing-parameter case is caught at the boundary (D3).
If editors produce malformed rules in practice, 1d is the upgrade path (see *Revisit when*).

**Against 2a (expose `localeTag`):** option 2b keeps the contract ADR-0001 and the US-02 story
were written against: the API says `locale`, the domain says `locale`, and nobody downstream
needs to know about a Strapi naming restriction. 2a leaks a storage workaround into the public
wire contract for good, and any later consumer (another front end, an export) has to learn the
mapping too.

**Why we accept it:** making 2b complete means rewriting `locale` inside `sort` (string, array
and object forms) and inside arbitrarily nested `filters` (`$and`, `$or`, `$not`), on every
route that can reach `country` (including `filters[country][locale]` on `form-field`), and
keeping that in step with Strapi's query parser on each upgrade. It is also shadowed by Strapi's
own `locale` query parameter (`@strapi/utils@5.63.0` `dist/content-api-constants.js:14`). That is
exactly the bespoke code D4 asks us to avoid, for a cosmetic gain. The mapping in the front end is
one line in a parser that already exists.

### Confirmation

- Schema check (review checklist): `validation-rule.json` has no `json` attribute; `value` is
  `decimal`, `pattern` is `string`. `country/schema.json` has `localeTag` and no `locale`.
  `backend/src/api/country/controllers/country.ts` is the plain `createCoreController`.
- Runtime check (strapi-developer, recorded in the review response):
  `GET /api/countries?fields[0]=code&fields[1]=localeTag&sort=localeTag:asc&filters[localeTag][$eq]=es-CO`
  returns `200` with `localeTag: "es-CO"` and only CO.
- Unit tests: `country.spec.ts` (parser reads `localeTag`, drops an entry without it);
  `field-config.spec.ts` (a `pattern` rule reads `pattern`; a numeric rule reads a number
  `value`; a rule missing its kind's parameter makes the field malformed, per spec v0.4 AC-14).
- `grep -rn "'locale'" frontend/src/app/core` finds no `fields[...]=locale` request.

## Pros and Cons of the Options

### 1a. Typed attributes per parameter (chosen)

- Good, because the admin type-checks each parameter on save, and a regex is plain text.
- Good, because the change is one component file; the `rules` shape (repeatable component with
  `kind`) stays.
- Good, because no backend code is added (D4).
- Bad, because a missing parameter still saves; the boundary parser must catch it.
- Bad, because every rule shows all parameter inputs in the admin.

### 1b. Keep `json` and validate on save

- Good, because the schema does not change, and invalid values are rejected on save with an
  error the editor sees.
- Good, because the check could also cover a missing parameter and an invalid regex.
- Bad, because editors still type JSON, with quotes and doubled backslashes in a regex (against
  D1); the core complaint of F04 stays.
- Bad, because it adds a custom Document Service middleware or lifecycle on the write path, to
  test and re-verify on each upgrade (against D4).

### 1c. `string` `value` coerced by the front end

- Good, because a regex is plain text and the schema change is minimal.
- Bad, because a number is also free text: `"tres"` or `"3,5"` still saves and the field still
  disappears, so the wrong-type case of F04 is not solved (against D2).
- Bad, because the coercion rules (comma vs dot, spaces, `"03"`) become front-end logic that
  editors cannot see.

### 1d. One component per rule kind in a dynamic zone

Viable in 5.63.0 on the `form-field` content type only: the content-type builder lists
`dynamiczone` in the valid types for content types
(`@strapi/content-type-builder@5.63.0` `dist/server/controllers/validation/content-type.js:35-41`)
and not for components (`component.js:18-22`). Dynamic-zone entries carry `__component`
(`@strapi/utils@5.63.0` `dist/content-types.js`, `DYNAMIC_ZONE_KEYS`).

- Good, because each kind has only its own, required, typed parameters: a rule without its
  parameter cannot be saved.
- Good, because the admin shows a clear "add a rule of type X" picker.
- Bad, because `rules` changes from a repeatable component to a polymorphic list: new populate
  syntax, a `__component` discriminator in the parser, and a new seed and fixture shape.
- Bad, because adding a rule kind means a new component (schema plus code), not an enum value.
- Bad, because it is the largest change of the four, in a review-fix round.

### 2a. Expose `localeTag` (chosen)

- Good, because the stock controller handles `fields`, `sort` and `filters` (D5).
- Good, because it deletes the custom controller (D4).
- Bad, because the wire name differs from the domain name; the parser maps it.

### 2b. Keep and complete the renaming controller

- Good, because the API keeps the name `locale` from ADR-0001 and the US-02 story.
- Bad, because a complete rename covers `sort` and nested `filters` on every route that reaches
  `country`, and must track Strapi's query parsing (against D4).
- Bad, because `locale` is also Strapi's own query parameter, so the name stays ambiguous in the
  API.

### 2c. Another attribute name (for example `numberLocale`)

- Good, because the stock controller works, as in 2a, and the name may describe the purpose
  better.
- Bad, because the implementation, seed, fixtures and spec v0.4 already use `localeTag`; a
  different name is churn with no functional gain.
- Neutral: functionally equivalent to 2a.

## More Information

- **`locale` is reserved in Strapi 5.63.0** (verified in the installed packages, 5.63.0 per their
  `package.json`):
  - `@strapi/utils@5.63.0` `dist/content-types.js:51-76`, `RESERVED_ATTRIBUTE_NAMES` contains
    `'locale'` (line 69); `isReservedAttributeName` and `getReservedAttributeNames` use it, and
    the content-type builder refuses it (`@strapi/content-type-builder@5.63.0`
    `dist/server/services/builder.js:11`, `dist/server/controllers/validation/model-schema.js:73-85`,
    "Attribute keys cannot be one of …").
  - `@strapi/utils@5.63.0` `dist/content-api-constants.js:8-23`: `locale` is one of the shared
    content-API and Document Service query parameter keys.
  - `@strapi/core@5.63.0` `dist/services/document-service/repository.js:83-132` validates and
    normalises a `locale` parameter on every Document Service call, and
    `dist/utils/transform-content-types-to-models.js:365-372` treats a `locale` attribute as the
    i18n system column in the document index.
  - The 400 on `fields[]=locale`, `sort=locale` and `filters[locale]` with the attribute stored as
    `localeTag` comes from the field validator: `@strapi/utils@5.63.0`
    `dist/validate/validators.js:393-407` throws `Invalid key` for a key that is not a scalar
    attribute of the schema.
- Review evidence: `reviews/US-01-review-R1.md`, US-01-R1-F04 and US-01-R1-F05.
- Related ADRs: ADR-0001 (amended by this ADR, in the two points above only), ADR-0002 (public
  `country.find`, unchanged), ADR-0005 (same "less bespoke backend code" reasoning).
- Revisit when: editors save rules without their parameter more than occasionally (move to 1d), a
  rule kind needs more than one parameter of a new type, or a second consumer of the country API
  needs the name `locale` (then 2b, or an API version).

9	# ADR-0005: Scope of the temporary e2e API token when the created content has relations (amends ADR-0002)
10	
11	## Context and Problem Statement
12	
13	ADR-0002 (Accepted) lets the AC-03 end-to-end test create a `form-field` through Strapi's own port
14	with a temporary `custom` API token scoped to `api::form-field.form-field.create` and `.delete`
15	only (ADR-0002, "End-to-end writes for AC-03", step 3). A `form-field` has a required `country`
16	relation (ADR-0001). In gate attempt 1 of US-01, `POST /api/form-fields` with
17	`country: { connect: [<documentId>] }` failed with `400 ValidationError "Invalid key country"`
18	(`details.key = "country"`, `source = "body"`). Strapi 5.63.0 refuses a relation key in the
19	input unless the caller may **read** the relation target. The strapi-developer confirmed at runtime
20	that the same payload succeeds once `api::country.country.find` is added to the token. This ADR
21	decides how the e2e write gets past that check. It amends ADR-0002 **only** in the scope of the
22	temporary e2e token. Everything else in ADR-0002 stays as it is. Story: US-01
23	(`specs/US-01/spec.md`, US-01-AC-03, US-01-Q-23).
24	
25	## Decision Drivers
26	
27	- D1. "No Strapi token with write permissions may reach the browser. Public role permissions minimal and justified" (source: Assessment, security; CLAUDE.md §3; ADR-0002 D1). Any write credential stays minimal and lives only in the Playwright Node process.
28	- D2. AC-03 is automated: the test creates a published field linked to a country during the run, then deletes it (US-01-AC-03, US-01-Q-23).
29	- D3. Keep bespoke code off security-relevant paths: every custom controller on a write endpoint has to be reviewed and re-verified on each Strapi upgrade (human decision, Felipe Sabogal, 2026-11-21; ADR-0002 already carries one such custom piece, the published-only middleware).
30	- D4. Do not change the public role or the read path decided in ADR-0002 (Accepted ADRs are binding, CLAUDE.md §1).
31	
32	## Considered Options
33	
34	1. **Widen the temporary token**: `form-field.create`, `form-field.delete` and
35	   `api::country.country.find` (read-only).
36	2. **Custom `form-field` create controller**: validate the payload without `country`, then attach
37	   one validated country `documentId` before calling the document service; the token keeps the
38	   ADR-0002 scope. Implemented in commit e5ba5ff, to be reverted.
39	3. **Admin API (content-manager) write path**: no content-API token at all; the test uses the admin
40	   JWT it already obtains in ADR-0002 step 2 and calls
41	   `POST /content-manager/collection-types/api::form-field.form-field/actions/publish` (create and
42	   publish in one request) and `DELETE /content-manager/collection-types/api::form-field.form-field/:id`.
43	
44	## Decision Outcome
45	
46	Chosen option: **"1. Widen the temporary token with `country.find`"**, because it uses Strapi's
47	own relation-permission rule as designed and needs no custom code on a write endpoint (D3). The
48	only right it adds is a read of country data, which the public role already exposes (D1). The
49	AC-03 test then works with the stock controller (D2), and the public role and read path are
50	unchanged (D4).
51	
52	### What is decided (amendment to ADR-0002, step 3 of "End-to-end writes for AC-03")
53	
54	- The temporary `custom` API token created by the AC-03 test setup has exactly these permissions:
55	  `api::form-field.form-field.create`, `api::form-field.form-field.delete` and
56	  `api::country.country.find`. Nothing else. Lifespan and teardown stay as in ADR-0002 (7 days,
57	  deleted in teardown, also on failure).
58	- The custom `create` in `backend/src/api/form-field/controllers/form-field.ts` added by e5ba5ff
59	  is reverted to `factories.createCoreController('api::form-field.form-field')`.
60	- General rule for later stories: when a test token must write a document with relations, it gets
61	  `find` on each relation target, and on nothing more. ADR-0002's public role table does not
62	  change.
63	
64	### Consequences
65	
66	- Good, because the form-field write path is Strapi's stock controller again: input validation,
67	  sanitisation and the relation check all run unchanged (D3).
68	- Good, because the added permission matches what is already public. `api::country.country.find`
69	  is in the public role (ADR-0002 table), so the token learns nothing about published countries
70	  that an anonymous caller cannot learn.
71	- Bad, because the token's scope is no longer "write only". It now includes a read, and later
72	  stories will add one `find` per relation target (for example US-02 if a plan test writes plans
73	  with a `country` relation). Mitigation: the scope list sits in one place in the e2e setup, and
74	  review checks it against this ADR.
75	- Bad, because a token holder can read **draft** countries. The published-only middleware
76	  (`backend/src/middlewares/published-only.ts`) keeps publication parameters on any request that
77	  carries an `Authorization` header, so `GET /api/countries?status=draft` with this token returns
78	  drafts, which the public role cannot see. Mitigation: the token exists only in the Playwright
79	  Node process for the length of the test, is deleted in teardown, and country records hold no
80	  secret data (code, name, currency, locale).
81	- Neutral: Strapi checks the **token's own** permissions, not the public role's
82	  (`content-api-token.js` `verify`, see More Information). The public `country.find` therefore does
83	  not satisfy the check, and the token needs the permission itself.
84	
85	### Strongest argument against
86	
87	Option 3 removes the content-API write token altogether. ADR-0002 step 2 already logs in to the
88	admin API and holds an admin JWT in the Node process, and the content-manager can create, publish
89	and delete the field with that JWT. So there would be no token to scope, nothing to widen as
90	later stories add relations, no API token row to clean up, and the test would follow the same
91	path an editor takes in the admin panel, which is what AC-03 describes ("the business team adds
92	and publishes in Strapi a new field"). Option 1 keeps a second credential and adds to its scope.
93	
94	**Why we accept it:** the admin JWT belongs to the bootstrap super admin, so it has every admin
95	permission. Making it the write credential swaps a narrow, expiring, deletable token for a
96	full-power session, which is worse under D1. The content-manager routes are also internal admin
97	APIs whose payload format (relation `connect` shapes, locale and status handling) is less
98	documented than the REST API, the same risk ADR-0002 accepted only for `/admin/login` and
99	`/admin/api-tokens`. Option 1 grants a read on data that is already public and keeps the test on
100	the content API that ADR-0002 chose. Option 3 stays the fallback if the token scope grows beyond a
101	few `find` permissions.
102	
103	### Confirmation
104	
105	- E2E `frontend/e2e/us-01-config-change.spec.ts` (AC-03): the token creation request lists exactly
106	  the three permissions above; the test creates the `mobilePhone` field with
107	  `country: { connect: [<documentId>] }` through the stock controller and gets `201`; teardown
108	  deletes the field and the token.
109	- Review checklist: `backend/src/api/form-field/controllers/form-field.ts` is the plain
110	  `createCoreController` (no custom `create`); the e2e token scope matches this ADR; the token and
111	  admin JWT never enter the browser context (ADR-0002 confirmation still applies).
112	
113	## Pros and Cons of the Options
114	
115	### 1. Widen the temporary token with `country.find` (chosen)
116	
117	- Good, because no custom code: Strapi's own `throwRestrictedRelations` check passes the normal
118	  way.
119	- Good, because the added right is read-only and matches the public role.
120	- Bad, because the scope grows with every relation target a test writes to.
121	- Bad, because the token can read draft countries (mitigated above).
122	
123	### 2. Custom `form-field` create controller (commit e5ba5ff)
124	
125	The controller pulls `country` out of `data`, runs `validateInput` and `sanitizeInput` on the
126	rest, then passes `country: <documentId>` straight to the document service.
127	
128	- Good, because the token keeps the narrowest scope ADR-0002 wrote down (create and delete only).
129	- Good, because the document service still refuses an unknown `documentId`.
130	- Bad, because it deliberately bypasses Strapi's relation-permission check on a public write
131	  endpoint, for every caller that has `form-field.create`, not only the test. Any future token or
132	  role with that permission can then link a `form-field` to a country it cannot read.
133	- Bad, because it is bespoke security-relevant code (about 50 lines, its own relation-shape
134	  parser) to re-verify on every Strapi upgrade, against D3.
135	- Bad, because the same workaround would be needed again for every relation and every type a
136	  later test writes.
137	
138	### 3. Admin API (content-manager) write path
139	
140	Verified viable in `@strapi/content-manager@5.63.0`: `dist/server/routes/admin.js` defines
141	`POST /collection-types/:model/actions/publish` (handler `collection-types.publish`, policies
142	`admin::isAuthenticatedAdmin` and `explorer.publish`), and `dist/server/controllers/collection-types.js`
143	`publish` creates the document when no `id` is given ("Create a new document and publish it in one
144	request"). `DELETE /collection-types/:model/:id` maps to `collection-types.delete`. These routes are
145	served under the `/content-manager` prefix on the admin API.
146	
147	- Good, because no content-API write token exists at all, so there is nothing to scope or widen.
148	- Good, because it follows the same path an editor's click in the admin panel takes.
149	- Bad, because the credential is the super admin's JWT, with full admin rights, instead of a narrow
150	  expiring token (D1).
151	- Bad, because the content-manager API is internal to the admin panel and less documented, and its
152	  relation payload format was not exercised in this project.
153	- Bad, because it contradicts the write flow in ADR-0002 (steps 3 to 5) far more than a scope
154	  change does, so it would need a superseding ADR rather than an amendment.
155	
156	## More Information
157	
158	- Verified sources (2026-11-21; each package fetched with `npm pack` into a temporary directory
159	  outside the repo):
160	  - `@strapi/utils@5.63.0` `dist/validate/visitors/throw-restricted-relations.js`:
161	    `ACTIONS_TO_VERIFY = ['find']`; for a regular relation, `handleRegularRelation` builds the
162	    scope `` `${attribute.target}.find` `` and calls `strapi.auth.verify(auth, { scope })`; if it
163	    fails, `throwInvalidKey({ key, path })` raises the observed `Invalid key country`
164	    (`dist/validate/utils.js`, `throwInvalidKey`).
165	  - `@strapi/utils@5.63.0` `dist/validate/index.js` `validateInput`: the restricted-relations
166	    visitor runs whenever the request has `auth` (`if (auth) { transforms.push(traverseEntity(throwRestrictedRelations(auth), …)) }`).
167	  - `@strapi/core@5.63.0` `dist/core-api/controller/collection-type.js` `create` calls
168	    `this.validateInput(body.data, ctx)`, which delegates to `strapi.contentAPI.validate.input`
169	    (`dist/core-api/controller/index.js`).
170	  - `@strapi/admin@5.63.0` `dist/server/server/src/strategies/content-api-token.js` `verify`: for a
171	    `custom` token, `scopes.every((scope) => ability.can(scope))`, so only the token's own
172	    permissions count (the public role is not consulted).
173	  - `@strapi/content-manager@5.63.0` `dist/server/routes/admin.js` and
174	    `dist/server/controllers/collection-types.js` (option 3, cited above).
175	- Runtime evidence (strapi-developer, gate attempt 1): the 400 body quoted in the context, and the
176	  `201` once `country.find` was added to the token.
177	- Related ADRs: ADR-0002 (amended here, only step 3 of the AC-03 write flow; its index status
178	  becomes "Accepted (amended by ADR-0005)"), ADR-0001 (the `country` relation on per-country
179	  types).
180	- Revisit when: a test token needs `find` on a type that is not in the public role, the scope list
181	  grows beyond a handful of `find` permissions (then reconsider option 3 in a superseding ADR), or a
182	  Strapi upgrade changes `ACTIONS_TO_VERIFY` or the token `verify` logic.

# ADR-0005: Scope of the temporary e2e API token when the created content has relations (amends ADR-0002)

## Context and Problem Statement

ADR-0002 (Accepted) lets the AC-03 end-to-end test create a `form-field` through Strapi's own port
with a temporary `custom` API token scoped to `api::form-field.form-field.create` and `.delete`
only (ADR-0002, "End-to-end writes for AC-03", step 3). A `form-field` has a required `country`
relation (ADR-0001). In gate attempt 1 of US-01, `POST /api/form-fields` with
`country: { connect: [<documentId>] }` failed with `400 ValidationError "Invalid key country"`
(`details.key = "country"`, `source = "body"`). Strapi 5.63.0 refuses a relation key in the
input unless the caller may **read** the relation target. The strapi-developer confirmed at runtime
that the same payload succeeds once `api::country.country.find` is added to the token. This ADR
decides how the e2e write gets past that check. It amends ADR-0002 **only** in the scope of the
temporary e2e token. Everything else in ADR-0002 stays as it is. Story: US-01
(`specs/US-01/spec.md`, US-01-AC-03, US-01-Q-23).

## Decision Drivers

- D1. "No Strapi token with write permissions may reach the browser. Public role permissions minimal and justified" (source: Assessment, security; CLAUDE.md §3; ADR-0002 D1). Any write credential stays minimal and lives only in the Playwright Node process.
- D2. AC-03 is automated: the test creates a published field linked to a country during the run, then deletes it (US-01-AC-03, US-01-Q-23).
- D3. Keep bespoke code off security-relevant paths: every custom controller on a write endpoint has to be reviewed and re-verified on each Strapi upgrade (human decision, Felipe Sabogal, 2026-11-21; ADR-0002 already carries one such custom piece, the published-only middleware).
- D4. Do not change the public role or the read path decided in ADR-0002 (Accepted ADRs are binding, CLAUDE.md §1).

## Considered Options

1. **Widen the temporary token**: `form-field.create`, `form-field.delete` and
   `api::country.country.find` (read-only).
2. **Custom `form-field` create controller**: validate the payload without `country`, then attach
   one validated country `documentId` before calling the document service; the token keeps the
   ADR-0002 scope. Implemented in commit e5ba5ff, to be reverted.
3. **Admin API (content-manager) write path**: no content-API token at all; the test uses the admin
   JWT it already obtains in ADR-0002 step 2 and calls
   `POST /content-manager/collection-types/api::form-field.form-field/actions/publish` (create and
   publish in one request) and `DELETE /content-manager/collection-types/api::form-field.form-field/:id`.

## Decision Outcome

Chosen option: **"1. Widen the temporary token with `country.find`"**, because it uses Strapi's
own relation-permission rule as designed and needs no custom code on a write endpoint (D3). The
only right it adds is a read of country data, which the public role already exposes (D1). The
AC-03 test then works with the stock controller (D2), and the public role and read path are
unchanged (D4).

### What is decided (amendment to ADR-0002, step 3 of "End-to-end writes for AC-03")

- The temporary `custom` API token created by the AC-03 test setup has exactly these permissions:
  `api::form-field.form-field.create`, `api::form-field.form-field.delete` and
  `api::country.country.find`. Nothing else. Lifespan and teardown stay as in ADR-0002 (7 days,
  deleted in teardown, also on failure).
- The custom `create` in `backend/src/api/form-field/controllers/form-field.ts` added by e5ba5ff
  is reverted to `factories.createCoreController('api::form-field.form-field')`.
- General rule for later stories: when a test token must write a document with relations, it gets
  `find` on each relation target, and on nothing more. ADR-0002's public role table does not
  change.

### Consequences

- Good, because the form-field write path is Strapi's stock controller again: input validation,
  sanitisation and the relation check all run unchanged (D3).
- Good, because the added permission matches what is already public. `api::country.country.find`
  is in the public role (ADR-0002 table), so the token learns nothing about published countries
  that an anonymous caller cannot learn.
- Bad, because the token's scope is no longer "write only". It now includes a read, and later
  stories will add one `find` per relation target (for example US-02 if a plan test writes plans
  with a `country` relation). Mitigation: the scope list sits in one place in the e2e setup, and
  review checks it against this ADR.
- Bad, because a token holder can read **draft** countries. The published-only middleware
  (`backend/src/middlewares/published-only.ts`) keeps publication parameters on any request that
  carries an `Authorization` header, so `GET /api/countries?status=draft` with this token returns
  drafts, which the public role cannot see. Mitigation: the token exists only in the Playwright
  Node process for the length of the test, is deleted in teardown, and country records hold no
  secret data (code, name, currency, locale).
- Neutral: Strapi checks the **token's own** permissions, not the public role's
  (`content-api-token.js` `verify`, see More Information). The public `country.find` therefore does
  not satisfy the check, and the token needs the permission itself.

### Strongest argument against

Option 3 removes the content-API write token altogether. ADR-0002 step 2 already logs in to the
admin API and holds an admin JWT in the Node process, and the content-manager can create, publish
and delete the field with that JWT. So there would be no token to scope, nothing to widen as
later stories add relations, no API token row to clean up, and the test would follow the same
path an editor takes in the admin panel, which is what AC-03 describes ("the business team adds
and publishes in Strapi a new field"). Option 1 keeps a second credential and adds to its scope.

**Why we accept it:** the admin JWT belongs to the bootstrap super admin, so it has every admin
permission. Making it the write credential swaps a narrow, expiring, deletable token for a
full-power session, which is worse under D1. The content-manager routes are also internal admin
APIs whose payload format (relation `connect` shapes, locale and status handling) is less
documented than the REST API, the same risk ADR-0002 accepted only for `/admin/login` and
`/admin/api-tokens`. Option 1 grants a read on data that is already public and keeps the test on
the content API that ADR-0002 chose. Option 3 stays the fallback if the token scope grows beyond a
few `find` permissions.

### Confirmation

- E2E `frontend/e2e/us-01-config-change.spec.ts` (AC-03): the token creation request lists exactly
  the three permissions above; the test creates the `mobilePhone` field with
  `country: { connect: [<documentId>] }` through the stock controller and gets `201`; teardown
  deletes the field and the token.
- Review checklist: `backend/src/api/form-field/controllers/form-field.ts` is the plain
  `createCoreController` (no custom `create`); the e2e token scope matches this ADR; the token and
  admin JWT never enter the browser context (ADR-0002 confirmation still applies).

## Pros and Cons of the Options

### 1. Widen the temporary token with `country.find` (chosen)

- Good, because no custom code: Strapi's own `throwRestrictedRelations` check passes the normal
  way.
- Good, because the added right is read-only and matches the public role.
- Bad, because the scope grows with every relation target a test writes to.
- Bad, because the token can read draft countries (mitigated above).

### 2. Custom `form-field` create controller (commit e5ba5ff)

The controller pulls `country` out of `data`, runs `validateInput` and `sanitizeInput` on the
rest, then passes `country: <documentId>` straight to the document service.

- Good, because the token keeps the narrowest scope ADR-0002 wrote down (create and delete only).
- Good, because the document service still refuses an unknown `documentId`.
- Bad, because it deliberately bypasses Strapi's relation-permission check on a public write
  endpoint, for every caller that has `form-field.create`, not only the test. Any future token or
  role with that permission can then link a `form-field` to a country it cannot read.
- Bad, because it is bespoke security-relevant code (about 50 lines, its own relation-shape
  parser) to re-verify on every Strapi upgrade, against D3.
- Bad, because the same workaround would be needed again for every relation and every type a
  later test writes.

### 3. Admin API (content-manager) write path

Verified viable in `@strapi/content-manager@5.63.0`: `dist/server/routes/admin.js` defines
`POST /collection-types/:model/actions/publish` (handler `collection-types.publish`, policies
`admin::isAuthenticatedAdmin` and `explorer.publish`), and `dist/server/controllers/collection-types.js`
`publish` creates the document when no `id` is given ("Create a new document and publish it in one
request"). `DELETE /collection-types/:model/:id` maps to `collection-types.delete`. These routes are
served under the `/content-manager` prefix on the admin API.

- Good, because no content-API write token exists at all, so there is nothing to scope or widen.
- Good, because it follows the same path an editor's click in the admin panel takes.
- Bad, because the credential is the super admin's JWT, with full admin rights, instead of a narrow
  expiring token (D1).
- Bad, because the content-manager API is internal to the admin panel and less documented, and its
  relation payload format was not exercised in this project.
- Bad, because it contradicts the write flow in ADR-0002 (steps 3 to 5) far more than a scope
  change does, so it would need a superseding ADR rather than an amendment.

## More Information

- Verified sources (2026-11-21; each package fetched with `npm pack` into a temporary directory
  outside the repo):
  - `@strapi/utils@5.63.0` `dist/validate/visitors/throw-restricted-relations.js`:
    `ACTIONS_TO_VERIFY = ['find']`; for a regular relation, `handleRegularRelation` builds the
    scope `` `${attribute.target}.find` `` and calls `strapi.auth.verify(auth, { scope })`; if it
    fails, `throwInvalidKey({ key, path })` raises the observed `Invalid key country`
    (`dist/validate/utils.js`, `throwInvalidKey`).
  - `@strapi/utils@5.63.0` `dist/validate/index.js` `validateInput`: the restricted-relations
    visitor runs whenever the request has `auth` (`if (auth) { transforms.push(traverseEntity(throwRestrictedRelations(auth), …)) }`).
  - `@strapi/core@5.63.0` `dist/core-api/controller/collection-type.js` `create` calls
    `this.validateInput(body.data, ctx)`, which delegates to `strapi.contentAPI.validate.input`
    (`dist/core-api/controller/index.js`).
  - `@strapi/admin@5.63.0` `dist/server/server/src/strategies/content-api-token.js` `verify`: for a
    `custom` token, `scopes.every((scope) => ability.can(scope))`, so only the token's own
    permissions count (the public role is not consulted).
  - `@strapi/content-manager@5.63.0` `dist/server/routes/admin.js` and
    `dist/server/controllers/collection-types.js` (option 3, cited above).
- Runtime evidence (strapi-developer, gate attempt 1): the 400 body quoted in the context, and the
  `201` once `country.find` was added to the token.
- Related ADRs: ADR-0002 (amended here, only step 3 of the AC-03 write flow; its index status
  becomes "Accepted (amended by ADR-0005)"), ADR-0001 (the `country` relation on per-country
  types).
- Revisit when: a test token needs `find` on a type that is not in the public role, the scope list
  grows beyond a handful of `find` permissions (then reconsider option 3 in a superseding ADR), or a
  Strapi upgrade changes `ACTIONS_TO_VERIFY` or the token `verify` logic.

9	# ADR-0006: Strapi physical model adjustments: typed validation-rule parameters and the country `localeTag` attribute (amends ADR-0001)
10	
11	## Context and Problem Statement
12	
13	ADR-0001 (Accepted) fixes the Strapi model for US-01. Code review round 1 found two places where
14	the implementation departs from it, or from spec §7.1, without a recorded decision:
15	
16	1. **Rule parameters (US-01-R1-F04).** `form.validation-rule` stores the parameter of
17	   `minLength`, `maxLength`, `min`, `max` and `pattern` in a free `json` attribute `value`
18	   (`backend/src/components/form/validation-rule.json`). Spec §7.1 says the rule kinds are
19	   "structured, not free JSON". Editors must type JSON (a regex needs quotes and doubled
20	   backslashes), and a value of the wrong type saves without error and then makes the front-end
21	   boundary parser drop the **whole field** (`frontend/src/app/shared/field-config.ts`), so a
22	   required reserved field such as `plate` can silently disappear from the form.
23	2. **Country locale (US-01-R1-F05).** ADR-0001 names the BCP 47 attribute of `country` `locale`.
24	   `locale` is a reserved attribute name in Strapi 5 (verified below), so commit 241340a stores
25	   it as `localeTag` and adds a custom `find` controller
26	   (`backend/src/api/country/controllers/country.ts`) that renames it back to `locale`, but only
27	   for `fields`. `sort=locale:asc` and `filters[locale][$eq]=es-CO` return
28	   `400 Invalid key locale` (reproduced by the reviewer). US-02 will consume this attribute for
29	   currency and number formatting.
30	
31	The human (Felipe Sabogal, 2026-11-21) decided the direction of both points after the review.
32	This ADR records the options and the decision. It amends **only** these two points of
33	ADR-0001's "What is decided → Strapi model"; everything else in ADR-0001 stays as written.
34	Story: US-01 (`specs/US-01/spec.md` §7.1, §7.3).
35	
36	## Decision Drivers
37	
38	- D1. "The business team, which is not technical, must be able to change the form fields and the offered plans from Strapi without requesting a deployment." (source: Assessment, business context; US-01-BR-06). An editor must be able to enter a rule parameter without knowing JSON syntax or escaping.
39	- D2. Rule kinds are "structured, not free JSON" (source: spec §7.1); "Editors must not be able to save something the frontend cannot parse" (source: `strapi-content-modeling` skill, modeling conventions).
40	- D3. A malformed configuration is not rendered and the app keeps working (source: US-01-Q-18, US-01-AC-14). The boundary parser stays the last line of defence, whatever the schema.
41	- D4. Keep bespoke backend code to a minimum: each custom controller or middleware must be reviewed and re-verified on every Strapi upgrade (source: human decision, Felipe Sabogal, 2026-11-21, the same reasoning recorded as D3 in ADR-0005).
42	- D5. The country attribute that carries the number locale must be fully usable through the stock content API: `fields`, `sort` and `filters` (source: US-01-R1-F05; US-02 story, "The price is shown in the country's currency and format").
43	- D6. Decisions are recorded and accepted ADRs are not rewritten (source: CLAUDE.md §1; `adr-madr` skill lifecycle).
44	
45	## Considered Options
46	
47	Point 1, rule parameters (`form.validation-rule`):
48	
49	1. **1a. Typed attributes per parameter** on the one component: numeric `value`, string
50	   `pattern`, integers `years`, `maxYearsOld`, `maxYearsAhead`; unused ones are null.
51	2. **1b. Keep the `json` `value`** and add server-side validation on save (a Document Service
52	   middleware or lifecycle that rejects a value of the wrong type for the rule `kind`).
53	3. **1c. A `string` `value`** that editors type as plain text, coerced to a number by the
54	   front-end parser for numeric kinds.
55	4. **1d. One component per rule kind in a dynamic zone** (`rules` becomes a `dynamiczone` on
56	   `form-field` with components such as `rule.min-length`, `rule.pattern`, `rule.min-age`,
57	   `rule.year-range`, `rule.rut-check-digit`, each with only its own, required, parameters).
58	
59	Point 2, country locale attribute:
60	
61	1. **2a. Expose `localeTag` as is**: the stored attribute and the API field are both
62	   `localeTag`; the front-end boundary parser maps it to its internal `locale`. The custom
63	   `find` controller is removed.
64	2. **2b. Keep the renaming controller and complete it**: also translate `sort` and `filters`
65	   (and any nested form of them) from `locale` to `localeTag`.
66	3. **2c. Another attribute name** chosen for readability (for example `numberLocale` or
67	   `formatLocale`), exposed as is.
68	
69	## Decision Outcome
70	
71	Chosen options: **"1a. Typed attributes per parameter"** and **"2a. Expose `localeTag` as is"**.
72	
73	1a, because each parameter gets a Strapi type the admin enforces on save (a number field cannot
74	hold `"tres"`, a regex is typed as plain text with no escaping), which meets D1 and D2 with a
75	one-file schema change and no custom backend code (D4), while keeping one repeatable component
76	and the current `rules` shape that the front end, seed and tests already use. 2a, because it uses
77	the stock controller, so `fields`, `sort` and `filters` all work (D5), and it removes custom code
78	instead of extending it (D4).
79	
80	### What is decided (amendment to ADR-0001, "What is decided → Strapi model")
81	
82	**`form.validation-rule` component** (`backend/src/components/form/validation-rule.json`):
83	
84	| Attribute | Strapi type | Used by kind | Notes |
85	|---|---|---|---|
86	| `kind` | `enumeration` (unchanged) | all | Required. `minLength`, `maxLength`, `min`, `max`, `pattern`, `minAge`, `yearRange`, `rutCheckDigit`. |
87	| `value` | `decimal` (replaces `json`) | `minLength`, `maxLength`, `min`, `max` | Numeric. Integer ≥ 0 for `minLength`/`maxLength` (checked at the boundary). |
88	| `pattern` | `string` (new) | `pattern` | ECMAScript regex source, no flags, typed as plain text. |
89	| `years` | `integer`, `min: 1` (unchanged) | `minAge` | |
90	| `maxYearsOld` | `integer`, `min: 0` (unchanged) | `yearRange` | |
91	| `maxYearsAhead` | `integer`, `min: 0` (unchanged) | `yearRange` | |
92	| `message` | `string` (unchanged) | all | Optional rule-specific message. |
93	
94	- Parameters a kind does not use are left empty and arrive as `null`. Strapi cannot make an
95	  attribute required depending on `kind`, so the front-end boundary parser still checks that the
96	  kind's own parameter is present and in range. The rule semantics of spec §7.1 do not change;
97	  only where the `pattern` parameter lives changes (`pattern` instead of `value`). The exact
98	  wire shape, and how a non-null unused parameter is treated, are fixed in spec v0.4.
99	- The seed (`backend/src/seed/form-fields.ts`), the annex `specs/US-01/seed-fields.md`, the
100	  front-end parser and its fixtures, and the AC-03 e2e payload move the regex from `value` to
101	  `pattern`.
102	- `decimal` was chosen over `float` because both are read back as a JavaScript number
103	  (`@strapi/database@5.63.0` `dist/fields/index.js:26-27` maps `float` and `decimal` to
104	  `NumberField`, whose `fromDB` returns `_.toNumber(value)`; `dist/query/helpers/transform.js:21`
105	  keeps `null` as `null`), and `decimal` stores values such as `0.1` exactly in the database.
106	
107	**`country` content type** (`backend/src/api/country/content-types/country/schema.json`):
108	
109	- The BCP 47 attribute is named **`localeTag`** (string, required), in storage and on the wire.
110	  ADR-0001's `locale` is replaced by `localeTag` everywhere it refers to the Strapi attribute
111	  (the model list, and the "narrow `fields[]`" request of the chooser, which asks for
112	  `localeTag`).
113	- `backend/src/api/country/controllers/country.ts` goes back to
114	  `factories.createCoreController('api::country.country')`.
115	- The front-end boundary parser (`frontend/src/app/shared/country.ts`) reads `localeTag` from the
116	  response and maps it to the internal `Country.locale` (or another internal name the spec
117	  chooses). Validation of the value is unchanged.
118	- ADR-0002's public role table still holds: `api::country.country.find` exposes "country code,
119	  name, currency, locale", and the locale is now carried by `localeTag`.
120	
121	### Consequences
122	
123	- Good, because an editor types `3` into a number field and `^[A-Za-z]{3}[0-9]{3}$` into a text
124	  field; Strapi refuses a non-number in `value` on save (`@strapi/core@5.63.0`
125	  `dist/services/entity-validator/validators.js:329-364`: `decimal` uses `floatValidator`,
126	  `yup.number()` with a finite-number test), so the wrong-type case of F04 can no longer reach
127	  the front end (D1, D2).
128	- Good, because both points end with **less** custom backend code: the country controller is
129	  deleted and no validation middleware is added (D4).
130	- Good, because `localeTag` works with every stock query parameter (`fields`, `sort`, `filters`),
131	  so US-02 can filter or sort on it without new backend work (D5).
132	- Bad, because a rule can still be saved without the parameter its kind needs (for example
133	  `minLength` with an empty `value`, or `pattern` with an invalid regex), and the boundary
134	  parser then drops the field — mitigation: the component's admin description lists which
135	  attribute each kind uses (as today), the parser logs a warning without user data (US-01-Q-18),
136	  and spec v0.4 keeps the malformed-rule cases in AC-14. 1d would remove the missing-parameter
137	  case; see *Strongest argument against*.
138	- Bad, because the component has fields that are meaningless for most kinds, and the admin shows
139	  all of them for every rule — mitigation: per-attribute descriptions; acceptable with eight
140	  kinds.
141	- Bad, because the wire name `localeTag` differs from the conceptual name in ADR-0001 and the
142	  US-02 story ("locale") — mitigation: the rename is confined to the boundary parser; this ADR
143	  and spec v0.4 record it.
144	- Bad, because existing development databases hold rule rows with the old `json` `value` and
145	  country rows that are already correct; the idempotent seed only creates missing items, so it
146	  will not rewrite old rule rows — mitigation: development data is disposable; reset the Strapi
147	  volume (or delete the seeded fields) after the schema change, and state this in the commit.
148	- Neutral: the public and e2e permissions of ADR-0002 and ADR-0005 do not change.
149	
150	### Strongest argument against
151	
152	**Against 1a (typed attributes):** option 1d makes invalid rules impossible to save, not merely
153	less likely. With one component per kind in a dynamic zone, each component carries only its own
154	parameters, marked `required`, so the admin will not save a `minLength` rule without a length, and
155	editors never see `years` next to a regex. Option 1a keeps a "pick a kind, then guess which of
156	five fields to fill" form, in which a missing parameter still saves and still makes the field
157	vanish from step 1, the exact failure mode F04 complained about, only narrower.
158	
159	**Why we accept it:** 1d is viable in Strapi 5.63.0 only on the content type (the content-type
160	builder allows `dynamiczone` for content types but not inside components:
161	`@strapi/content-type-builder@5.63.0` `dist/server/controllers/validation/content-type.js:35-41`
162	vs `component.js:18-22`), so it replaces `rules` with a polymorphic list of eight components. Every
163	response item gains a `__component` discriminator, the populate needs the fragment syntax
164	(`populate[rules][on][...]`, validated in `@strapi/utils@5.63.0` `dist/validate/validators.js:621`),
165	the boundary parser, seed, fixtures and AC-03 payload change shape, and a new rule kind becomes a
166	new component rather than a new enum value. That is a large change to code that passed every
167	other review item, made in a fix round. 1a removes the reported wrong-type and escaping problems
168	with one schema edit, and the remaining missing-parameter case is caught at the boundary (D3).
169	If editors produce malformed rules in practice, 1d is the upgrade path (see *Revisit when*).
170	
171	**Against 2a (expose `localeTag`):** option 2b keeps the contract ADR-0001 and the US-02 story
172	were written against: the API says `locale`, the domain says `locale`, and nobody downstream
173	needs to know about a Strapi naming restriction. 2a leaks a storage workaround into the public
174	wire contract for good, and any later consumer (another front end, an export) has to learn the
175	mapping too.
176	
177	**Why we accept it:** making 2b complete means rewriting `locale` inside `sort` (string, array
178	and object forms) and inside arbitrarily nested `filters` (`$and`, `$or`, `$not`), on every
179	route that can reach `country` (including `filters[country][locale]` on `form-field`), and
180	keeping that in step with Strapi's query parser on each upgrade. It is also shadowed by Strapi's
181	own `locale` query parameter (`@strapi/utils@5.63.0` `dist/content-api-constants.js:14`). That is
182	exactly the bespoke code D4 asks us to avoid, for a cosmetic gain. The mapping in the front end is
183	one line in a parser that already exists.
184	
185	### Confirmation
186	
187	- Schema check (review checklist): `validation-rule.json` has no `json` attribute; `value` is
188	  `decimal`, `pattern` is `string`. `country/schema.json` has `localeTag` and no `locale`.
189	  `backend/src/api/country/controllers/country.ts` is the plain `createCoreController`.
190	- Runtime check (strapi-developer, recorded in the review response):
191	  `GET /api/countries?fields[0]=code&fields[1]=localeTag&sort=localeTag:asc&filters[localeTag][$eq]=es-CO`
192	  returns `200` with `localeTag: "es-CO"` and only CO.
193	- Unit tests: `country.spec.ts` (parser reads `localeTag`, drops an entry without it);
194	  `field-config.spec.ts` (a `pattern` rule reads `pattern`; a numeric rule reads a number
195	  `value`; a rule missing its kind's parameter makes the field malformed, per spec v0.4 AC-14).
196	- `grep -rn "'locale'" frontend/src/app/core` finds no `fields[...]=locale` request.
197	
198	## Pros and Cons of the Options
199	
200	### 1a. Typed attributes per parameter (chosen)
201	
202	- Good, because the admin type-checks each parameter on save, and a regex is plain text.
203	- Good, because the change is one component file; the `rules` shape (repeatable component with
204	  `kind`) stays.
205	- Good, because no backend code is added (D4).
206	- Bad, because a missing parameter still saves; the boundary parser must catch it.
207	- Bad, because every rule shows all parameter inputs in the admin.
208	
209	### 1b. Keep `json` and validate on save
210	
211	- Good, because the schema does not change, and invalid values are rejected on save with an
212	  error the editor sees.
213	- Good, because the check could also cover a missing parameter and an invalid regex.
214	- Bad, because editors still type JSON, with quotes and doubled backslashes in a regex (against
215	  D1); the core complaint of F04 stays.
216	- Bad, because it adds a custom Document Service middleware or lifecycle on the write path, to
217	  test and re-verify on each upgrade (against D4).
218	
219	### 1c. `string` `value` coerced by the front end
220	
221	- Good, because a regex is plain text and the schema change is minimal.
222	- Bad, because a number is also free text: `"tres"` or `"3,5"` still saves and the field still
223	  disappears, so the wrong-type case of F04 is not solved (against D2).
224	- Bad, because the coercion rules (comma vs dot, spaces, `"03"`) become front-end logic that
225	  editors cannot see.
226	
227	### 1d. One component per rule kind in a dynamic zone
228	
229	Viable in 5.63.0 on the `form-field` content type only: the content-type builder lists
230	`dynamiczone` in the valid types for content types
231	(`@strapi/content-type-builder@5.63.0` `dist/server/controllers/validation/content-type.js:35-41`)
232	and not for components (`component.js:18-22`). Dynamic-zone entries carry `__component`
233	(`@strapi/utils@5.63.0` `dist/content-types.js`, `DYNAMIC_ZONE_KEYS`).
234	
235	- Good, because each kind has only its own, required, typed parameters: a rule without its
236	  parameter cannot be saved.
237	- Good, because the admin shows a clear "add a rule of type X" picker.
238	- Bad, because `rules` changes from a repeatable component to a polymorphic list: new populate
239	  syntax, a `__component` discriminator in the parser, and a new seed and fixture shape.
240	- Bad, because adding a rule kind means a new component (schema plus code), not an enum value.
241	- Bad, because it is the largest change of the four, in a review-fix round.
242	
243	### 2a. Expose `localeTag` (chosen)
244	
245	- Good, because the stock controller handles `fields`, `sort` and `filters` (D5).
246	- Good, because it deletes the custom controller (D4).
247	- Bad, because the wire name differs from the domain name; the parser maps it.
248	
249	### 2b. Keep and complete the renaming controller
250	
251	- Good, because the API keeps the name `locale` from ADR-0001 and the US-02 story.
252	- Bad, because a complete rename covers `sort` and nested `filters` on every route that reaches
253	  `country`, and must track Strapi's query parsing (against D4).
254	- Bad, because `locale` is also Strapi's own query parameter, so the name stays ambiguous in the
255	  API.
256	
257	### 2c. Another attribute name (for example `numberLocale`)
258	
259	- Good, because the stock controller works, as in 2a, and the name may describe the purpose
260	  better.
261	- Bad, because the implementation, seed, fixtures and spec v0.4 already use `localeTag`; a
262	  different name is churn with no functional gain.
263	- Neutral: functionally equivalent to 2a.
264	
265	## More Information
266	
267	- **`locale` is reserved in Strapi 5.63.0** (verified in the installed packages, 5.63.0 per their
268	  `package.json`):
269	  - `@strapi/utils@5.63.0` `dist/content-types.js:51-76`, `RESERVED_ATTRIBUTE_NAMES` contains
270	    `'locale'` (line 69); `isReservedAttributeName` and `getReservedAttributeNames` use it, and
271	    the content-type builder refuses it (`@strapi/content-type-builder@5.63.0`
272	    `dist/server/services/builder.js:11`, `dist/server/controllers/validation/model-schema.js:73-85`,
273	    "Attribute keys cannot be one of …").
274	  - `@strapi/utils@5.63.0` `dist/content-api-constants.js:8-23`: `locale` is one of the shared
275	    content-API and Document Service query parameter keys.
276	  - `@strapi/core@5.63.0` `dist/services/document-service/repository.js:83-132` validates and
277	    normalises a `locale` parameter on every Document Service call, and
278	    `dist/utils/transform-content-types-to-models.js:365-372` treats a `locale` attribute as the
279	    i18n system column in the document index.
280	  - The 400 on `fields[]=locale`, `sort=locale` and `filters[locale]` with the attribute stored as
281	    `localeTag` comes from the field validator: `@strapi/utils@5.63.0`
282	    `dist/validate/validators.js:393-407` throws `Invalid key` for a key that is not a scalar
283	    attribute of the schema.
284	- Review evidence: `reviews/US-01-review-R1.md`, US-01-R1-F04 and US-01-R1-F05.
285	- Related ADRs: ADR-0001 (amended by this ADR, in the two points above only), ADR-0002 (public
286	  `country.find`, unchanged), ADR-0005 (same "less bespoke backend code" reasoning).
287	- Revisit when: editors save rules without their parameter more than occasionally (move to 1d), a
288	  rule kind needs more than one parameter of a new type, or a second consumer of the country API
289	  needs the name `locale` (then 2b, or an API version).

8	
9	# ADR-0005: Scope of the temporary e2e API token when the created content has relations (amends ADR-0002)
10	
11	## Context and Problem Statement
12	
13	ADR-0002 (Accepted) lets the AC-03 end-to-end test create a `form-field` through Strapi's own port
14	with a temporary `custom` API token scoped to `api::form-field.form-field.create` and `.delete`
15	only (ADR-0002, "End-to-end writes for AC-03", step 3). A `form-field` has a required `country`
16	relation (ADR-0001). In gate attempt 1 of US-01, `POST /api/form-fields` with
17	`country: { connect: [<documentId>] }` failed with `400 ValidationError "Invalid key country"`
18	(`details.key = "country"`, `source = "body"`). Strapi 5.63.0 refuses a relation key in the
19	input unless the caller may **read** the relation target. The strapi-developer confirmed at runtime
20	that the same payload succeeds once `api::country.country.find` is added to the token. This ADR
21	decides how the e2e write gets past that check. It amends ADR-0002 **only** in the scope of the
22	temporary e2e token. Everything else in ADR-0002 stays as it is. Story: US-01
23	(`specs/US-01/spec.md`, US-01-AC-03, US-01-Q-23).
24	
25	## Decision Drivers
26	
27	- D1. "No Strapi token with write permissions may reach the browser. Public role permissions minimal and justified" (source: Assessment, security; CLAUDE.md §3; ADR-0002 D1). Any write credential stays minimal and lives only in the Playwright Node process.
28	- D2. AC-03 is automated: the test creates a published field linked to a country during the run, then deletes it (US-01-AC-03, US-01-Q-23).
29	- D3. Keep bespoke code off security-relevant paths: every custom controller on a write endpoint has to be reviewed and re-verified on each Strapi upgrade (human decision, Felipe Sabogal, 2026-11-21; ADR-0002 already carries one such custom piece, the published-only middleware).
30	- D4. Do not change the public role or the read path decided in ADR-0002 (Accepted ADRs are binding, CLAUDE.md §1).
31	
32	## Considered Options
33	
34	1. **Widen the temporary token**: `form-field.create`, `form-field.delete` and
35	   `api::country.country.find` (read-only).
36	2. **Custom `form-field` create controller**: validate the payload without `country`, then attach
37	   one validated country `documentId` before calling the document service; the token keeps the
38	   ADR-0002 scope. Implemented in commit e5ba5ff, to be reverted.
39	3. **Admin API (content-manager) write path**: no content-API token at all; the test uses the admin
40	   JWT it already obtains in ADR-0002 step 2 and calls
41	   `POST /content-manager/collection-types/api::form-field.form-field/actions/publish` (create and
42	   publish in one request) and `DELETE /content-manager/collection-types/api::form-field.form-field/:id`.
43	
44	## Decision Outcome
45	
46	Chosen option: **"1. Widen the temporary token with `country.find`"**, because it uses Strapi's
47	own relation-permission rule as designed and needs no custom code on a write endpoint (D3). The
48	only right it adds is a read of country data, which the public role already exposes (D1). The
49	AC-03 test then works with the stock controller (D2), and the public role and read path are
50	unchanged (D4).
51	
52	### What is decided (amendment to ADR-0002, step 3 of "End-to-end writes for AC-03")
53	
54	- The temporary `custom` API token created by the AC-03 test setup has exactly these permissions:
55	  `api::form-field.form-field.create`, `api::form-field.form-field.delete` and
56	  `api::country.country.find`. Nothing else. Lifespan and teardown stay as in ADR-0002 (7 days,
57	  deleted in teardown, also on failure).
58	- The custom `create` in `backend/src/api/form-field/controllers/form-field.ts` added by e5ba5ff
59	  is reverted to `factories.createCoreController('api::form-field.form-field')`.
60	- General rule for later stories: when a test token must write a document with relations, it gets
61	  `find` on each relation target, and on nothing more. ADR-0002's public role table does not
62	  change.
63	
64	### Consequences
65	
66	- Good, because the form-field write path is Strapi's stock controller again: input validation,
67	  sanitisation and the relation check all run unchanged (D3).
68	- Good, because the added permission matches what is already public. `api::country.country.find`
69	  is in the public role (ADR-0002 table), so the token learns nothing about published countries
70	  that an anonymous caller cannot learn.
71	- Bad, because the token's scope is no longer "write only". It now includes a read, and later
72	  stories will add one `find` per relation target (for example US-02 if a plan test writes plans
73	  with a `country` relation). Mitigation: the scope list sits in one place in the e2e setup, and
74	  review checks it against this ADR.
75	- Bad, because a token holder can read **draft** countries. The published-only middleware
76	  (`backend/src/middlewares/published-only.ts`) keeps publication parameters on any request that
77	  carries an `Authorization` header, so `GET /api/countries?status=draft` with this token returns
78	  drafts, which the public role cannot see. Mitigation: the token exists only in the Playwright
79	  Node process for the length of the test, is deleted in teardown, and country records hold no
80	  secret data (code, name, currency, locale).
81	- Neutral: Strapi checks the **token's own** permissions, not the public role's
82	  (`content-api-token.js` `verify`, see More Information). The public `country.find` therefore does
83	  not satisfy the check, and the token needs the permission itself.
84	
85	### Strongest argument against
86	
87	Option 3 removes the content-API write token altogether. ADR-0002 step 2 already logs in to the
88	admin API and holds an admin JWT in the Node process, and the content-manager can create, publish
89	and delete the field with that JWT. So there would be no token to scope, nothing to widen as
90	later stories add relations, no API token row to clean up, and the test would follow the same
91	path an editor takes in the admin panel, which is what AC-03 describes ("the business team adds
92	and publishes in Strapi a new field"). Option 1 keeps a second credential and adds to its scope.
93	
94	**Why we accept it:** the admin JWT belongs to the bootstrap super admin, so it has every admin
95	permission. Making it the write credential swaps a narrow, expiring, deletable token for a
96	full-power session, which is worse under D1. The content-manager routes are also internal admin
97	APIs whose payload format (relation `connect` shapes, locale and status handling) is less
98	documented than the REST API, the same risk ADR-0002 accepted only for `/admin/login` and
99	`/admin/api-tokens`. Option 1 grants a read on data that is already public and keeps the test on
100	the content API that ADR-0002 chose. Option 3 stays the fallback if the token scope grows beyond a
101	few `find` permissions.
102	
103	### Confirmation
104	
105	- E2E `frontend/e2e/us-01-config-change.spec.ts` (AC-03): the token creation request lists exactly
106	  the three permissions above; the test creates the `mobilePhone` field with
107	  `country: { connect: [<documentId>] }` through the stock controller and gets `201`; teardown
108	  deletes the field and the token.
109	- Review checklist: `backend/src/api/form-field/controllers/form-field.ts` is the plain
110	  `createCoreController` (no custom `create`); the e2e token scope matches this ADR; the token and
111	  admin JWT never enter the browser context (ADR-0002 confirmation still applies).
112	
113	## Pros and Cons of the Options
114	
115	### 1. Widen the temporary token with `country.find` (chosen)
116	
117	- Good, because no custom code: Strapi's own `throwRestrictedRelations` check passes the normal
118	  way.
119	- Good, because the added right is read-only and matches the public role.
120	- Bad, because the scope grows with every relation target a test writes to.
121	- Bad, because the token can read draft countries (mitigated above).
122	
123	### 2. Custom `form-field` create controller (commit e5ba5ff)
124	
125	The controller pulls `country` out of `data`, runs `validateInput` and `sanitizeInput` on the
126	rest, then passes `country: <documentId>` straight to the document service.
127	
128	- Good, because the token keeps the narrowest scope ADR-0002 wrote down (create and delete only).
129	- Good, because the document service still refuses an unknown `documentId`.
130	- Bad, because it deliberately bypasses Strapi's relation-permission check on a public write
131	  endpoint, for every caller that has `form-field.create`, not only the test. Any future token or
132	  role with that permission can then link a `form-field` to a country it cannot read.
133	- Bad, because it is bespoke security-relevant code (about 50 lines, its own relation-shape
134	  parser) to re-verify on every Strapi upgrade, against D3.
135	- Bad, because the same workaround would be needed again for every relation and every type a
136	  later test writes.
137	
138	### 3. Admin API (content-manager) write path
139	
140	Verified viable in `@strapi/content-manager@5.63.0`: `dist/server/routes/admin.js` defines
141	`POST /collection-types/:model/actions/publish` (handler `collection-types.publish`, policies
142	`admin::isAuthenticatedAdmin` and `explorer.publish`), and `dist/server/controllers/collection-types.js`
143	`publish` creates the document when no `id` is given ("Create a new document and publish it in one
144	request"). `DELETE /collection-types/:model/:id` maps to `collection-types.delete`. These routes are
145	served under the `/content-manager` prefix on the admin API.
146	
147	- Good, because no content-API write token exists at all, so there is nothing to scope or widen.
148	- Good, because it follows the same path an editor's click in the admin panel takes.
149	- Bad, because the credential is the super admin's JWT, with full admin rights, instead of a narrow
150	  expiring token (D1).
151	- Bad, because the content-manager API is internal to the admin panel and less documented, and its
